definition_zh: 在环境方面；环保地；以对环境无害的方式；就周围环境而言；从环境影响角度看；由环境引起地
definition_en: in relation to the natural environment; in a way that protects or harms the environment; with respect to surrounding conditions; from the standpoint of environmental impact; as caused by external conditions
core_image: 一只手把垃圾分成两堆，又把可回收的那堆送进循环箱：同一个动作，结果分到两个未来
scene: 顾客自带杯子买咖啡。 The customer brings a cup for coffee, and the barista says this way of ordering is more environmentally friendly.
sceneCN: 这里 environmentally 是「环保地、对环境友好地」（第 2 个义项：以保护环境的方式）；句意：顾客自带杯子买咖啡，店员说这样点单对环境更友好。图中可辨识物件：自带杯、咖啡机、循环使用标识、店员的手。

pos.zh: 在环境方面；环保地（修饰形容词或动词，如 environmentally friendly）

collocations.zh: 环境无害的；环境上可靠的

senses.title: In relation to the natural environment
senses.definition: in a way that relates to the natural world and its condition
senses.definitionCN: 以与自然世界及其状况相关的方式
senses.example: The two proposals should be compared environmentally, not only financially.
senses.exampleCN: 这两项提案应比较其环境方面，而不仅是财务方面。
senses.why: Environmentally is environmental + -ly, where -ly comes from Old English -lice. The adverb puts the adjective into the frame 'with respect to X': it does not describe an action's manner so much as the dimension on which it is judged.
senses.whyCN: environmentally 是 environmental + -ly，其中 -ly 来自古英语 -lice。这个副词把形容词放进“就 X 而言”的框架：它与其说描述动作方式，不如说指示评判的维度。

senses.title: In a way that protects nature
senses.definition: in a manner that reduces harm to or improves the natural environment
senses.definitionCN: 以减少对自然环境的损害或改善自然环境的方式
senses.example: The building is heated environmentally, using solar gain and ground-source heat.
senses.exampleCN: 这栋建筑用太阳能得热与地源热来供暖，方式是环保的。
senses.why: This is the everyday 'green' use, fixed in the phrase environmentally friendly. The adverb modifies an adjective and signals a value judgment: the action is measured against its ecological cost.
senses.whyCN: 这是日常的“环保”用法，固定在 environmentally friendly 短语中。副词修饰形容词并传递价值判断：该行为要按生态代价来衡量。

senses.title: With respect to surroundings
senses.definition: in relation to the surrounding conditions of a place, organism, or system
senses.definitionCN: 与某地点、生物或系统的周围条件相关
senses.example: The species is environmentally adapted to cold, wet summers.
senses.exampleCN: 该物种在环境上适应寒冷潮湿的夏季。
senses.why: This sense is neutral and scientific: the surroundings can be a climate or a laboratory chamber. The adverb marks the dimension of adaptation, not a moral claim about protecting nature.
senses.whyCN: 这个义项中性而科学：周围可以是气候或实验舱。副词标记的是适应维度，而不是保护自然的道德主张。

senses.title: From the standpoint of impact
senses.definition: judged by the effect an action has on the environment
senses.definitionCN: 按某行为对环境造成的效果来评判
senses.example: The route is environmentally expensive because it cuts through a wetland.
senses.exampleCN: 这条路线在环境上代价高昂，因为它穿过湿地。
senses.why: Here the adverb introduces a cost-benefit frame: the environment becomes one column in an evaluation. It often pairs with expensive, costly, damaging, or beneficial.
senses.whyCN: 这里副词引入成本—收益框架：环境成为评估中的一栏。它常与 expensive、costly、damaging、beneficial 搭配。

senses.title: As caused by external conditions
senses.definition: as produced by surrounding conditions rather than by genes or internal causes
senses.definitionCN: 由周围条件而非基因或内部原因造成
senses.example: The disorder is environmentally triggered but genetically predisposed.
senses.exampleCN: 这种障碍由环境触发，但有遗传易感性。
senses.why: Biology uses the adverb to assign causation: an environmentally induced effect comes from outside the organism. The word marks a cause, not a setting, which is why it can stand before induced or triggered.
senses.whyCN: 生物学用这个副词来归因：environmentally induced 的效应来自生物体之外。这个词标记原因而非场景，所以能放在 induced、triggered 之前。

senses.title: In environmental design terms
senses.definition: in terms of how a building, product, or space is designed to relate to its surroundings
senses.definitionCN: 就建筑、产品或空间如何与其周围发生关系的设计而言
senses.example: The pavilion was environmentally designed to shade its own courtyard.
senses.exampleCN: 这座亭子在环境设计上是为了给自己的庭院遮阴。
senses.why: Design usage keeps both senses at once: the surroundings are physical, and the aim is low impact. The adverb describes an integrated approach rather than a single green feature.
senses.whyCN: 设计用法同时保留两层：周围是物理的，目标是低影响。副词描述的是一种整合方法，而非单一环保功能。

senses.title: In regulatory terms
senses.definition: in terms of environmental law, permits, or official standards
senses.definitionCN: 就环境法、许可或官方标准而言
senses.example: The site is environmentally compliant but socially contested.
senses.exampleCN: 该场址在环境法规上是合规的，但在社会层面有争议。
senses.why: Law and compliance use the adverb to locate a claim inside a regulatory frame: compliant, permitted, approved. The environment becomes a set of standards rather than a physical place.
senses.whyCN: 法律与合规用这个副词把主张放进监管框架：compliant、permitted、approved。环境变成一套标准，而非一个物理场所。

senses.title: From an ecological viewpoint in an argument
senses.definition: speaking from an ecological point of view, often to introduce a contrast
senses.definitionCN: 从生态观点出发说话，常引出对照
senses.example: Environmentally, the plan is sound; economically, it is fragile.
senses.exampleCN: 从环境角度看，该计划可靠；从经济角度看，它很脆弱。
senses.why: Sentence-initial use makes the adverb a frame-setter, like 'economically' or 'technically'. It tells the listener which dimension the next claim is measured on, and it often sets up a contrast with another dimension.
senses.whyCN: 置于句首时，这个副词是框架设定语，类似 economically、technically。它告诉听者接下来的主张按哪个维度衡量，且常与另一个维度形成对照。

intro.en: Environmentally is environmental + -ly. Environmental is environment + -al, and environment is environ 'to surround' + -ment, from Old French environ 'around'. The adverb's -ly goes back to Old English -lice, so this is a layered English construction on a French-derived noun of uncertain deeper origin.
intro.cn: environmentally 是 environmental + -ly。environmental 是 environment + -al，而 environment 是 environ“包围”+ -ment，来自古法语 environ“在周围”。副词后缀 -ly 上溯古英语 -lice，因此这是一个在法语来源名词上层层构成的英语派生词，其更深词源不确定。

items.en: Old French environ 'around' came from en- 'in' plus viron 'circuit'. The verb environner 'to surround' produced the noun environnement.
items.cn: 古法语 environ“在周围”来自 en-“在内”加 viron“环、圈”。动词 environner“包围”产生名词 environnement。

items.en: The deeper origin of viron is uncertain; a link with virer 'to turn' is plausible but the etymology of virer is itself disputed. No reliable Latin source is asserted here.
items.cn: viron 的更早来源不确定；与 virer“转动”的联系有可能，但 virer 的词源本身有争议。此处不断言可靠的拉丁来源。

items.en: English environment entered in the seventeenth century and settled into the modern sense of surrounding conditions by the nineteenth. Environmental followed as its adjective.
items.cn: 英语 environment 于 17 世纪进入，到 19 世纪定型为“周围状况”的现代义。environmental 随后作为其形容词出现。

items.en: The adverb environmentally is a straightforward -ly formation on environmental. Its early uses concern surroundings generally, not ecology.
items.cn: 副词 environmentally 是在 environmental 上的直接 -ly 构成。其早期用法泛指周围，而非生态。

items.en: After the mid-twentieth century the adverb attached to 'friendly', 'sound', and 'sustainable', becoming a standard way to praise low ecological impact. The exact first appearance of environmentally friendly is uncertain.
items.cn: 20 世纪中叶以后，这个副词与 friendly、sound、sustainable 结合，成为称赞低生态影响的标准说法。environmentally friendly 的确切首现年代来源不确定。

items.en: Today the adverb works as a dimension marker in arguments: environmentally, economically, socially. That frame-setting use is the most abstract extension of 'surroundings'.
items.cn: 今天这个副词在论证中充当维度标记：environmentally、economically、socially。这种框架设定用法是“周围”最抽象的延伸。

note.en: The first group separates the environment family by suffix; the second group separates adverbs that also mark a dimension or manner.
note.cn: 第一组按后缀区分 environment 词族；第二组区分同样标记维度或方式的其他副词。

entries.definition: relating to the environment. It is the adjective that -ly turns into this adverb.
entries.definitionCN: 与环境相关的。它是被 -ly 转化为该副词的形容词。

entries.definition: the surroundings or conditions of something. It is the noun at the base of the whole family.
entries.definitionCN: 某物的周围状况或条件。它是整个词族底部的名词。

entries.definition: the movement or belief in protecting nature. The -ism suffix marks a doctrine, not a manner.
entries.definitionCN: 保护自然的运动或信念。-ism 后缀标记学说，而非方式。

entries.definition: from the standpoint of ecology as a science. It is more technical and less value-laden than environmentally.
entries.definitionCN: 从作为科学的生态学角度。它比 environmentally 更技术化、更少价值色彩。

entries.definition: in an environmentally friendly way. It is rare and informal, while environmentally is standard in policy and advertising.
entries.definitionCN: 以环保的方式。它罕用且口语化，而 environmentally 是政策与广告中的标准词。

entries.definition: in a way that does not exhaust resources. It stresses long-term use, while environmentally stresses ecological effect.
entries.definitionCN: 以不耗尽资源的方式。它强调长期使用，而 environmentally 强调生态影响。

normalIntro.en: Real associations: environment + -al + -ly, the fixed phrase environmentally friendly, and the sentence-initial frame 'environmentally, economically, socially'.
normalIntro.cn: 真实联想：environment + -al + -ly、固定短语 environmentally friendly，以及句首框架 environmentally、economically、socially。

normal.en: environment + -al + -ly: three suffixes stacked, each doing one job.
normal.cn: environment + -al + -ly：三个后缀叠加，各做一件事。

normal.en: -ly comes from Old English -lice, so the adverb layer is native even though the noun is French.
normal.cn: -ly 来自古英语 -lice，所以尽管名词是法语来源，副词层是本土的。

normal.en: Environmentally friendly is the phrase you will meet most; learn it as a unit.
normal.cn: environmentally friendly 是最常遇到的短语；把它当作一个整体记住。

normal.en: At the start of a sentence, environmentally picks the dimension of judgment, like economically or technically.
normal.cn: 在句首，environmentally 选定评判维度，类似 economically 或 technically。

normal.en: In biology, environmentally induced means the cause came from outside the organism.
normal.cn: 生物学中 environmentally induced 指原因来自生物体之外。

abstract.en: A dimension word does not describe; it decides what counts as success in the next clause.
abstract.cn: 维度词不描述，而是决定下一分句中什么算成功。

abstract.en: Surroundings enter the ledger twice: as a place to protect and as a cost to be counted.
abstract.cn: 周围在账本上出现两次：作为要保护的地方，也作为要计入的成本。

abstract.en: Doing something environmentally is doing it with the boundary of the system in view.
abstract.cn: 以环境方式做事，就是把系统的边界纳入视野。

examples.en: The packaging is environmentally friendly and can be composted at home.
examples.cn: 这种包装对环境友好，可在家堆肥。

examples.en: Environmentally, the dam is the costlier option; economically, it is the cheaper one.
examples.cn: 从环境角度看，大坝代价更高；从经济角度看，它更便宜。

examples.en: The crop's yield is environmentally limited by rainfall rather than by soil.
examples.cn: 该作物的产量受降雨而非土壤的环境限制。

dict_mnemonic.text: “因外绕，门头，利”——因为外面绕着门头的那圈东西有利，就要环保 → environmentally 在环境方面

root: environ（包围，古法语“在周围”）+ -ment（名词）+ -al（形容词）+ -ly（副词，古英语 -lice）；字面义“以包围着我们的一切为参照”，核心是“从环境这一维度”。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses of environmentally all select a dimension rather than describe a manner: natural condition, protection, surroundings, impact, external cause, design, regulation, or argumentative frame. The word tells the listener how the next claim is to be measured.
sensesIntro.cn: environmentally 的八个义项都在选定一个维度，而非描述方式：自然状况、保护、周围、影响、外部原因、设计、法规或论证框架。这个词告诉听者接下来的主张按什么衡量。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a pair of sorting hands that send one object into the recycling stream and another into waste — one action, two futures.
core.cn: 核心意象：一双分拣的手，把一个物件送进回收流，把另一个送进垃圾流——一个动作，两个未来。

branches.en: DIMENSION: a comparison, adaptation, or judgment is made with respect to the surroundings.
branches.cn: 维度：比较、适应或判断是就周围状况作出的。

branches.en: VALUE: the same dimension becomes a moral or cost judgment, praising low harm or counting high cost.
branches.cn: 价值：同一维度变成道德或成本判断，称赞低损害或计入高代价。

branches.en: CAUSE: in biology, the adverb assigns an external cause rather than a setting.
branches.cn: 原因：生物学中这个副词指派外部原因，而非场景。

branches.en: DESIGN AND LAW: the dimension is built into a product or fixed in a permit and a standard.
branches.cn: 设计与法律：这一维度被做进产品，或被固定在许可与标准中。

branches.en: FRAME: sentence-initial use sets the dimension for the whole claim, often in contrast with another.
branches.cn: 框架：句首用法为整个主张设定维度，常与另一维度对照。

intro.en: Environmentally is the adverb layer of a three-suffix family. The affix set shows the noun, adjective, adverb, doctrine, and person nouns, with -ly traced to Old English -lice.
intro.cn: environmentally 是一个三后缀词族的副词层。词缀组展示名词、形容词、副词、学说名词与人名词，并把 -ly 追溯到古英语 -lice。

latinIntro.en: Old French viron 'circle' and environ 'around' give the noun environment; English adds -al and then -ly. The deeper root of viron is uncertain, so no Latin entries are asserted.
latinIntro.cn: 古法语 viron“圈”与 environ“在周围”给出名词 environment；英语再加 -al 与 -ly。viron 的更早词根不确定，因此不断言拉丁条目。

definition_zh: n. 努力；尽力；尝试；（尤指长期的）事业 / v. 努力；尽力；力图
definition_en: an attempt to achieve something, especially one needing sustained effort, or to try hard to do something
core_image: 登山者在岩壁前反复试同一条路线，粉袋拍了又拍，笔记本上画满失败的箭头
scene: 登山者反复试同一条路线，笔记本上画满失败的箭头。 The climb was a long endeavour that took three seasons.
sceneCN: 这里 endeavour 指「长期的努力」（第 1 个义项：需要持续投入的尝试或事业）；句意是这次攀登是一项花了三个季度的长期努力。

senses.title: A sustained attempt
senses.definition: an attempt to achieve something that needs continued effort
senses.definitionCN: （名词）需要持续投入才能达成某事的尝试
senses.example: The climb was a long endeavour that took three seasons.
senses.exampleCN: 这次攀登是一项花了三个季度的长期努力。
senses.why: A notebook full of failed arrows beside a climber chalking the same hold again
senses.whyCN: 登山者又一次给同一个岩点抹粉，旁边笔记本上画满失败的箭头

senses.title: A field of human effort
senses.definition: a whole area of activity in which people try to achieve something
senses.definitionCN: （名词）人们在其中力求有所成就的一整个活动领域
senses.example: Space flight is a costly but shared human endeavour.
senses.exampleCN: 航天是一项代价高昂却由人类共同承担的事业。
senses.why: A launch pad watched by people from forty countries at once
senses.whyCN: 一座发射台，同时被四十个国家的人注视着

senses.title: To try hard
senses.definition: to try hard to do or achieve something
senses.definitionCN: （动词）努力去做或达成某事
senses.example: We shall endeavour to reply within five working days.
senses.exampleCN: 我们将力求在五个工作日内回复。
senses.why: A clerk rewriting the same reply until the wording is exact
senses.whyCN: 一位职员把同一封回信重写，直到措辞准确

intro.en: Endeavour is en- plus devoir, duty, from Old French deveir and Latin debere, to owe; to endeavour is to put yourself under a duty to do the thing.
intro.cn: endeavour 由 en- 加 devoir（职责）组成，devoir 来自古法语 deveir 与拉丁语 debere（欠）；endeavour 就是让自己背负起做这件事的责任。

items.en: Debere means to owe, and gives debt, debit and due.
items.cn: debere 意为欠，给出 debt、debit 与 due。

items.en: Deveir means duty or what one ought to do.
items.cn: deveir 意为职责、应当做的事。

items.en: Middle English endevoir means to put oneself under a duty.
items.cn: 中古英语 endevoir 意为使自己承担职责。

items.en: The spelling settles as endeavour in British use.
items.cn: 英式用法中拼写定为 endeavour。

items.en: American spelling drops the u, giving endeavor.
items.cn: 美式拼写去掉 u，成为 endeavor。

items.en: The noun is used of whole fields such as science and space flight.
items.cn: 名词用于指科学、航天等整个领域。

note.en: Endeavour comes from Latin debere, to owe, through French devoir, duty; debt, due and duty are cousins, while effort and attempt are the nearest synonyms.
note.cn: endeavour 经由法语 devoir（职责）来自拉丁语 debere（欠）；debt、due 与 duty 是同源表亲，而 effort 与 attempt 是最接近的同义词。

dict_mnemonic.text: endeavour ＝ en-（使进入）＋ deavour（职责，古法语 deveir，拉丁 debere「欠」）＝「使自己背负职责」→ 努力、尽力。美式拼写 endeavor，少一个 u。同根 debt 债务、debit 借方、due 应付的、duty 责任、devoir 职责。名词用法：a scientific endeavour 科学事业、human endeavour 人类的努力、a joint endeavour 共同的努力、make every endeavour 尽一切努力。动词用法：endeavour to do 力图做、endeavour to improve 力求改进，后接 to 不定式，语气比 try 正式。注意 endeavour 强调长期、持续、有分量的投入，attempt 只指一次尝试，effort 指使出的力气。

root: en-（使进入）＋ 拉丁语 debere（欠）→ 古法语 deveir（职责）→ endeavour（背负职责去努力）

sensesIntro.en: Three debts taken on: a climber chalking the same hold again, a launch pad watched by forty countries and a clerk rewriting one reply until it is exact.
sensesIntro.cn: 三种背下的债：又一次给同一岩点抹粉的登山者、被四十个国家注视的发射台，以及把一封回信改到准确的职员。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a notebook full of failed arrows beside a climber chalking the same hold again
core.cn: 核心意象：登山者又一次给同一个岩点抹粉，旁边笔记本上画满失败的箭头

branches.en: A duty carried through many tries.
branches.cn: 在多次尝试中扛起的职责。

branches.en: A duty shared by a whole field.
branches.cn: 由整个领域共担的职责。

branches.en: A duty expressed as trying hard.
branches.cn: 表现为尽力去做的职责。

branches.en: Both are larger than a single attempt.
branches.cn: 两者都比一次尝试更大。

branches.en: Both keep going after the first failure.
branches.cn: 两者都在第一次失败后继续。

intro.en: Endeavour is en- plus devoir; the owing root debere also gives debt, debit, due and duty.
intro.cn: endeavour 由 en- 加 devoir 组成；表「欠」的词根 debere 也给出 debt、debit、due 与 duty。

latinIntro.en: Latin debere means to owe, from de- plus habere, to have away; debitum is what is owed and gives debt and debit.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 debere 意为欠，由 de- 加 habere 构成，字面是把东西拿开；debitum 是所欠之物，给出 debt 与 debit。

definition_zh: 可协商的；可转让兑现的；可通行的
definition_en: open to being discussed and changed, able to be transferred to another holder, or able to be crossed
core_image: 价签旁用铅笔写了一行小字，意思是这数字还能动
scene: 拍卖行的图录上，底价旁边有一行铅笔小字，写着「可再议」。 The asking price is negotiable, so the buyer waited until the last hour to make an offer.
sceneCN: 这里 negotiable 指「条件可以再谈、不必照字面接受」（第 1 个义项：价格留有余地）；句意为要价可以商量，因此买家一直等到最后一个小时才出价。可辨识物件：图录、铅笔小字、价签、举牌。

pos.zh: （票据）可转让兑现的；（道路）可通行的

senses.title: A price left open to bargaining
senses.titleCN: 价格留有余地，可以再谈
senses.definition: of a price or fee, not fixed, so that an offer below it may be accepted
senses.definitionCN: 指价格或费用没有定死，低于标价的出价也可能被接受
senses.example: The fee is negotiable if the work is finished early.
senses.exampleCN: 如果能提前完工，费用可以商量。
senses.why: the suffix -able turns the bargaining verb into a property: what can be bargained over is negotiable.
senses.whyCN: 后缀 -able 把「讨价还价」这个动作变成一种性质：能拿去谈的，就是 negotiable。

senses.title: Terms open to adjustment
senses.titleCN: 条款可以经过商谈改动
senses.definition: of clauses in a contract, capable of being changed by discussion
senses.definitionCN: 指合同中的条款能够通过商谈修改
senses.example: Every clause is negotiable except the delivery date.
senses.exampleCN: 除交货日期外，每一条款都可以商量。
senses.why: a clause is negotiable when it is still on the table, and closed when the parties stop talking about it.
senses.whyCN: 条款只要还在桌上，就是可谈的；双方不再谈它，就成了定局。

senses.title: Paper that can change hands
senses.definition: of a cheque, bill or note, legally transferable to another holder
senses.definitionCN: 指支票、汇票或本票在法律上可以转给另一个持有人
senses.example: A negotiable instrument can be passed on by endorsement.
senses.exampleCN: 可流通票据能通过背书转让。
senses.why: commerce reuses the bargaining idea: a bill whose ownership can be handed over is a bill that can be dealt with.
senses.whyCN: 商业沿用「可谈」的思路：所有权能交出去的票据，就是能被处置的票据。

senses.title: A dispute that can be talked out
senses.titleCN: 争端可以通过谈判解决
senses.definition: of a conflict, capable of being settled by discussion rather than by force
senses.definitionCN: 指冲突能够通过商谈而非强制手段解决
senses.example: The dispute was negotiable, so no court action followed.
senses.exampleCN: 这场争议可以谈，因此没有走到诉讼。
senses.why: calling a dispute negotiable is a judgement about method: words may still work.
senses.whyCN: 说一场争端 negotiable，其实是在判断「办法」：话还管用。

senses.title: Ground that can be crossed
senses.definition: of a route, pass or slope, possible to travel over
senses.definitionCN: 指路线、隘口或坡面能够通行
senses.example: The pass is negotiable only from June to September.
senses.exampleCN: 这道隘口只有六月到九月可以通行。
senses.why: the physical branch of the verb survives here: what can be got through is literally negotiable.
senses.whyCN: 动词里那条「身体通过」的分支在此留存：能过得去的，字面上就是 negotiable。

senses.title: A person willing to bargain
senses.titleCN: 指人愿意谈、不把话堵死
senses.definition: of a person or a position, willing to discuss and give ground
senses.definitionCN: 指人或立场愿意商谈、肯作让步
senses.example: She remains negotiable on the price but not on the deadline.
senses.exampleCN: 她在价格上仍可谈，在期限上则不让步。
senses.why: the adjective shifts from the matter to the holder: a person is negotiable when nothing is shut.
senses.whyCN: 这个形容词从「事情」移到「持事的人」：人 negotiable，是说他没有把门关死。

senses.title: A draft that can be cashed
senses.definition: of a draft, able to be paid out or accepted for value at a bank
senses.definitionCN: 指汇票能在银行兑现或被承付
senses.example: Travellers may find the draft negotiable at any branch.
senses.exampleCN: 旅客会发现这张汇票在任何一家分行都能兑付。
senses.why: banks say a draft is negotiable when they will buy it, which is the transfer sense seen from the counter.
senses.whyCN: 银行说一张汇票 negotiable，意思是它愿意买下它；这是从柜台那一侧看到的「转让」义。

senses.title: A clause open to periodic review
senses.titleCN: 条款按固定周期可再议
senses.definition: of a rent or a royalty, subject to renegotiation at set intervals
senses.definitionCN: 指租金或提成按约定的周期可以重新商定
senses.example: The rent is negotiable every five years.
senses.exampleCN: 租金每五年可以重新议定一次。
senses.why: a review clause keeps an agreement deliberately unfinished, so the same adjective marks it.
senses.whyCN: 复审条款故意让协议「不封口」，于是同一个形容词也用来标记它。

intro.en: Negotiable is the Latin-derived bargaining verb plus -able, the ending that marks what can be done. It entered English through commercial law. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: negotiable 是那个源自拉丁语的「谈判」动词加上 -able 构成，后者标记「可以被做」；它经商业法进入英语。年代均为约数。

items.en: Negotium 'business' was built from neg- 'not' and otium 'leisure', so trade was described as the absence of free time.
items.cn: negotium「生意」由 neg-「不」与 otium「闲暇」构成，于是「买卖」被描述为「没有空闲」。

items.en: The verb negotiari meant 'to carry on business', and its participle supplied the stem used by English.
items.cn: 动词 negotiari 意为「经商」，其分词提供英语所用的词干。

items.en: The ending -abilis marked what can be done or what serves a purpose; through French it became the English -able that builds hundreds of adjectives.
items.cn: 词尾 -abilis 标记「可被做」或「可供使用」；经法语变为英语的 -able，构成数以百计的形容词。

items.en: The adjective appears in English commercial writing in the eighteenth century, first of bills and notes that could be transferred.
items.cn: 这个形容词在十八世纪的商业文书中出现，最初用于可以转让的汇票与本票。

items.en: From paper the word spread to prices, contracts and finally to roads and slopes that can be got through.
items.cn: 从票据出发，这个词扩展到价格、合同，最后扩展到能过得去的道路与坡面。

items.en: Source uncertain (first date): the earliest commercial citation is dated differently across dictionaries, and the deeper origin of otium is a reconstruction.
items.cn: 来源不确定（首见年代）：各家词典对最早的商业书证年代说法不一；otium 的更早来历属重构形式。

note.en: Group one holds words whose endings make them look like relatives of this one; group two holds adjectives with a genuinely similar reach.
note.cn: 第一组收因词尾相似而看来像本词亲属的词；第二组收意义上确实相近的形容词。

entries.definition: From Latin navigare 'to sail', built on navis 'ship' and agere 'drive': a river that ships can pass, not a price that can be argued.
entries.definitionCN: 来自拉丁 navigare「航行」，由 navis「船」与 agere「驾驶」构成：指可供船行的河，而非可议的价。

entries.definition: From negligere 'to disregard', built on legere 'to pick up'; it means too small to matter, with no bargaining sense.
entries.definitionCN: 来自 negligere「忽视」，由 legere「拾取」构成；意为小到可以忽略，与「谈判」无关。

entries.definition: The verb this adjective comes from: to bargain, or to get through a hard passage.
entries.definitionCN: 本形容词所出的动词：讨价还价，或通过难走的一段。

entries.definition: The noun for the talking itself; the adjective describes a property of what that talking can change.
entries.definitionCN: 指商谈这件事本身的名词；形容词则描述「被商谈改变」的那种性质。

entries.definition: Able to be altered without breaking; broader than negotiable, which needs two parties to agree.
entries.definitionCN: 能改动而不折断；比 negotiable 宽，后者需要双方同意。

entries.definition: Able to be handed to another owner; it covers only the commercial branch of negotiable.
entries.definitionCN: 能交给另一个所有者的；只覆盖 negotiable 的商业那一支。

entries.definition: Open to dispute rather than open to a deal; a debatable point may never be settled by bargaining.
entries.definitionCN: 可以争论，而不是可以成交；可争之点未必能靠谈判定下来。

entries.definition: Liable to change without anyone deciding; negotiable implies the change would come from agreement.
entries.definitionCN: 会自行变动；而 negotiable 暗示变动来自双方同意。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real fixed phrases and real word relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: Neg- 'not' plus otium 'leisure' gives the business stem, and -able adds 'can be'.
normal.cn: neg-「不」加 otium「闲暇」给出「生意」词干，-able 再加上「可以被」。

normal.en: The family runs negotiate, negotiation, negotiator, negotiable, negotiability, renegotiate.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 negotiate、negotiation、negotiator、negotiable、negotiability、renegotiate。

normal.en: Fixed phrases split into two fields: a negotiable price, a negotiable instrument.
normal.cn: 固定搭配分成两个领域：可议的价格、可流通的票据。

normal.en: The usual negation is not a prefix but the phrase not open to negotiation.
normal.cn: 常见的否定并不是加前缀，而是「不容商量」这一说法。

normal.en: The opposite adjective non-negotiable is common in politics and in contracts.
normal.cn: 相反的形容词 non-negotiable 在政治与合同中都很常见。

abstract.en: Picture a price tag written in pencil rather than ink.
abstract.cn: 想象一张用铅笔而不是墨水写的价签。

abstract.en: Picture a door whose hinge is loose enough to open a little wider.
abstract.cn: 想象一扇门的铰链松得还能再开一点。

abstract.en: Picture a rope bridge that sways but still carries a walker across.
abstract.cn: 想象一座会晃、却仍能把人送过对岸的索桥。

examples.en: The salary is negotiable, but the start date is not.
examples.cn: 薪资可以谈，入职日期不可以。

examples.en: Only the lower path is negotiable in winter.
examples.cn: 冬天只有下面那条小路能走。

examples.en: The note is negotiable at any bank in the city.
examples.cn: 这张本票在本市任何银行都可兑付。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「negotiate（谈判）+ able（能）」——能拿去谈的 → 可协商的

root: 拉丁 negotium（生意，字面「不得闲」）+ -abilis（可被……的）→ 英语 negotiable；商业法中最先指可转让票据，后扩展到价格、条款与可通行地形。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses all answer one question: can this still be moved? A price, a clause, a bill, a dispute, a pass, a person, a draft and a rent clause can each be moved in a different way.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项都在回答同一个问题：这东西还能不能动。价格、条款、票据、争端、隘口、人、汇票与租金条款，各自以不同方式「能动」。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a price tag written in pencil, with a small note in the margin saying it can still change.
core.cn: 核心意象：一张用铅笔写的价签，页边还有一行小字说这数字还能改。

branches.en: TALKABLE TERMS: a price and a clause stay unfinished while the parties keep talking.
branches.cn: 可谈的条款：只要双方还在谈，价格与条款就保持「未封口」。

branches.en: PAPER IN MOTION: a bill passes by endorsement, and a draft is bought at the counter.
branches.cn: 会动的纸：汇票靠背书传递，本票在柜台被买下。

branches.en: PEOPLE AND CONFLICTS: a quarrel can be talked out, and a person stays open to a deal.
branches.cn: 人与争端：争执可以谈开，人也始终留着成交的余地。

branches.en: GROUND: the old physical branch, where a pass opens for a few months each year.
branches.cn: 地形：最具体的一支，隘口每年只开放几个月。

branches.en: DELIBERATE GAP: a review clause keeps the agreement open on a schedule.
branches.cn: 刻意留的缝：复审条款按周期把协议重新打开。

intro.en: Negotiable is a Latin business noun turned into an adjective by a suffix that English borrowed and never stopped using.
intro.cn: negotiable 是一个拉丁「生意」名词，靠一个英语借来后一直沿用的后缀变成形容词。

latinIntro.en: The Latin noun negotium and the verb negotiari supply the stem, while -abilis supplies the meaning of possibility.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁名词 negotium 与动词 negotiari 提供词干，-abilis 提供「可能」之意。

items.example: Leisure is the second element of the compound.
The suffix turns a verb into a possibility.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀把动词变成一种可能性。

items.meaning: able to be bargained or transferred

items.exampleCN: 可流通性使这张本票有用。

items.example: The negotiator kept her voice low.
items.exampleCN: 谈判者把声音放得很低。
这条安全规定不容商量。

items.example: They renegotiate the rent every five years.
items.exampleCN: 他们每五年重谈一次租金。

latinEntries.structure: negotiari, negotiatus sum (deponent verb, first conjugation)

definition_zh: 理性；合理性；合乎逻辑的程度；理性思考能力
definition_en: the quality of being guided by reason, or the extent to which something can be justified by logic
core_image: 一个人在天平两端放上证据与反证，让指针慢慢停在正中
scene: 这里指「理性」。 Bounded rationality admits that real decisions are limited by time and incomplete information.
sceneCN: 这里 rationality 指「理性（有限理性理论中的决策理性）」（第 4 个义项：受时间与信息限制的理性）；句意：有限理性承认真实决策受时间与不完整信息限制。图中可辨识物件：天平、证据卡片、时钟、档案夹。

pos.zh: 理性；合理性；合乎逻辑；理性思考能力（多作不可数，指多种类型时可用复数 rationalities）

derivatives.zh: 理性主义者；理性主义的

senses.title: The capacity to reason
senses.titleCN: 理性能力：凭推理而非冲动行事的能力
senses.definition: the human capacity to think, weigh evidence and draw conclusions rather than act on impulse
senses.definitionCN: 人进行思考、权衡证据并得出结论、而非凭冲动行事的能力
senses.example: Rationality is what lets a child learn that a taller glass can hold less water.
senses.exampleCN: 理性让人能学会：更高的杯子未必装得下更多水。
senses.why: The noun is built on Latin ratio 'reckoning, reason', so rationality names the faculty of doing what ratio does: counting, comparing and concluding.
senses.whyCN: 该名词基于拉丁 ratio「计算、理性」，因此 rationality 命名的是执行 ratio 所做之事的能力：计数、比较与下结论。

senses.title: Logical consistency
senses.titleCN: 逻辑一致性：前提能否支撑结论
senses.definition: the property of an argument or belief whose parts support one another without contradiction
senses.definitionCN: 论证或信念的各部分互相支撑、不自相矛盾的性质
senses.example: The rationality of the argument depends on whether its premises really support the conclusion.
senses.exampleCN: 这个论证是否合理，取决于其前提是否真的支持结论。
senses.why: Here the word shifts from the thinker to the product: a set of statements can be called rational when its internal links hold.
senses.whyCN: 这里词义从思考者转向思考产物：一组陈述只要内部联系站得住，就可称为合理。

senses.title: Economic rational choice
senses.titleCN: 经济理性：按偏好选择最优方案
senses.definition: in economics, the assumption that agents choose the option that best satisfies their preferences given available information
senses.definitionCN: 经济学中假定行为者在既有信息下选择最能满足其偏好的方案
senses.example: Rationality in economics does not require perfect foresight, only consistent preferences.
senses.exampleCN: 经济学中的理性并不要求完美预见，只要求偏好一致。
senses.why: Model-builders narrowed ratio to a calculable rule: compare options, assign values, pick the highest. The noun then names that rule-following.
senses.whyCN: 建模者把 ratio 收窄为可计算的规则：比较选项、赋值、取最高者。该名词于是命名这种按规则行事。

senses.title: Bounded rationality
senses.titleCN: 有限理性：受时间与信息限制的理性
senses.definition: the theory that real decision-makers are rational only within limits set by time, information and mental capacity
senses.definitionCN: 认为真实决策者只在时间、信息与心智能力所设的界限内保持理性的理论
senses.example: Bounded rationality explains why managers satisfice instead of searching for the best option.
senses.exampleCN: 有限理性解释了管理者为何满足于够用方案，而不去搜寻最优选项。
senses.why: The phrase adds a boundary to the noun: reason still operates, but not with unlimited resources, so the result is 'good enough' rather than optimal.
senses.whyCN: 该短语给名词加上边界：理性仍在运作，但资源并非无限，因此结果只是「够用」而非最优。

senses.title: Justification by reasons
senses.titleCN: 理由正当性：信念或行动能否给出理由
senses.definition: in philosophy, the property of a belief or action that can be defended with reasons others could examine
senses.definitionCN: 哲学上指信念或行动能够用他人可检验的理由来辩护的性质
senses.example: Philosophers ask whether rationality alone can justify a moral belief.
senses.exampleCN: 哲学家追问单凭理性是否就能为道德信念提供正当性。
senses.why: Ratio also meant 'account' in the sense of a reckoning given to someone; rationality keeps that courtroom flavour of being answerable with reasons.
senses.whyCN: ratio 也有「向人交代的账目」之义；rationality 保留了这种「能用理由作答」的法庭气息。

senses.title: Formal and institutional rationality
senses.titleCN: 形式理性：制度按可计算规则运转
senses.definition: in social theory, especially Weber, the organization of action by calculable rules rather than tradition or personal whim
senses.definitionCN: 社会理论（尤其韦伯）中指按可计算规则、而非传统或个人任性来组织行动
senses.example: Weber saw formal rationality in bureaucracy, double-entry bookkeeping and the modern state.
senses.exampleCN: 韦伯在官僚制、复式记账与现代国家中看到了形式理性。
senses.why: Modern institutions extended ratio into rules and records; the noun then describes a system whose operations can be calculated in advance.
senses.whyCN: 现代制度把 ratio 扩展为规则与记录；该名词于是描述一种其运作可被预先计算的系统。

senses.title: Administrative overreach
senses.titleCN: 行政理性的反噬：规则僵化到违背目的
senses.definition: the quality of an organization that is highly rational in procedure but may lose sight of its purpose
senses.definitionCN: 组织在程序上高度理性、却可能偏离其目的的性质
senses.example: Critics warn that administrative rationality can produce rules that defeat their own aims.
senses.exampleCN: 批评者警告，行政理性可能造出违背自身目标的规则。
senses.why: This sense is rationality seen from outside: the machinery is consistent, yet the consistency itself becomes the problem.
senses.whyCN: 这一义项是从外部看理性：机器本身自洽，但自洽反而成了问题。

senses.title: Instrumental efficiency
senses.titleCN: 工具理性：只问手段是否高效
senses.definition: the kind of reason that asks how efficiently a goal can be reached, without judging whether the goal is worth reaching
senses.definitionCN: 只追问达成目标的手段是否高效、不评判目标本身是否值得追求的那种理性
senses.example: Instrumental rationality can build an efficient machine for a pointless task.
senses.exampleCN: 工具理性可以为一项无意义的任务造出高效的机器。
senses.why: The word separates means from ends: ratio calculates the shortest path, and the noun names that calculation when it is detached from value.
senses.whyCN: 该词把手段与目的分开：ratio 计算最短路径，名词命名的是这种与价值脱钩的计算。

intro.en: Rationality is a Latin-derived noun: ratio 'reckoning, reason' produced rationalis 'of reason', and Late Latin added -itas to make rationalitas. The English word appears in the sixteenth century.
intro.cn: rationality 是拉丁来源的名词：ratio「计算、理性」构成 rationalis「理性的」，晚期拉丁再加 -itas 造成 rationalitas。英语形式于 16 世纪出现。

items.en: Latin ratio meant 'a reckoning, account, calculation' and, by extension, 'reason'. It comes from ratus, the past participle of reri 'to reckon, think'. The deeper origin of reri is uncertain.
items.cn: 拉丁 ratio 意为「计算、账目、核算」，并引申为「理性」。它出自 reri「计算、思考」的过去分词 ratus。reri 的更深来源存疑。

items.en: Adding -alis produced rationalis 'belonging to reason, reasonable', the adjective behind English rational.
items.cn: 加上 -alis 构成 rationalis「属于理性的、合理的」，即英语 rational 背后的形容词。

items.en: Late Latin rationalitas named the quality of being reasonable. The suffix -itas is the ancestor of English -ity, which turns adjectives into names of qualities.
items.cn: 晚期拉丁 rationalitas 指「合理」这一性质。后缀 -itas 是英语 -ity 的前身，把形容词变成性质名词。

items.en: English rationality entered in the sixteenth century, first in theological and philosophical writing about reason and its limits.
items.cn: 英语 rationality 于 16 世纪进入，最早见于讨论理性及其限度的神学与哲学写作。

items.en: Economics, decision theory, sociology and law each narrowed the word: rational choice, bounded rationality, formal rationality and the rationality test.
items.cn: 经济学、决策理论、社会学与法学各自收窄了词义：理性选择、有限理性、形式理性与合理性审查。

items.en: The exact first English citation is uncertain, and any Indo-European root behind Latin reri would be a reconstruction rather than a recorded form.
items.cn: 来源不确定（更深词根）：英语最早书证确切年代存疑；拉丁 reri 背后的任何印欧词根都属于重构，而非有记录的形式。

note.en: The first group separates forms of the same ratio family; the second gives near-synonyms that stress logic, fairness or mental health.
note.cn: 第一组区分同一 ratio 词族的不同形式；第二组给出强调逻辑、公平或心智健全的近义词。

entries.definition: Meaning 'based on reason'. It describes a person or act, while rationality names the quality itself.
entries.definitionCN: 意为「基于理性的」，描述人或行为；rationality 则命名这种性质本身。

entries.definition: A noun for the underlying explanation or justification of something. It is not the quality of being rational.
entries.definitionCN: 指某事物背后的解释或理由，并非「理性的性质」。

entries.definition: The philosophical position that reason is the main source of knowledge. Rationality is the capacity; rationalism is a theory about it.
entries.definitionCN: 指认为理性是知识主要来源的哲学立场。rationality 是能力，rationalism 是关于该能力的理论。

entries.definition: To reorganize something on rational lines, or to invent a plausible excuse. Neither meaning is the noun rationality.
entries.definitionCN: 指按理性原则重组某物，或编造看似合理的借口；两者都不是名词 rationality。

entries.definition: The power of thinking, or a ground for a belief. Reason is broader and can be countable; rationality stresses consistency and justification.
entries.definitionCN: 指思维能力，或信念的依据。reason 范围更广且可数；rationality 更强调一致性与可辩护性。

entries.definition: The quality of being sensible and fair. It leans toward practical fairness, while rationality leans toward logical structure.
entries.definitionCN: 指通情达理与公平，偏向实践中的公允；rationality 偏向逻辑结构。

entries.definition: The system of valid inference, or the coherence of an argument. Logic is the tool; rationality is the broader disposition to use it.
entries.definitionCN: 指有效推理的规则体系，或论证的连贯性。logic 是工具，rationality 是更广的运用倾向。

entries.definition: A legal and medical word for a sound mind. It contrasts with illness, not with irrational argument.
entries.definitionCN: 法律与医学用语，指心智健全；它与疾病相对，而不是与不合逻辑的论证相对。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: ratio 'reckoning' + -ality: the quality of being able to reckon rightly.
normal.cn: ratio「核算」+ -ality：能够正确核算的性质。

normal.en: The family runs rational, rationally, rationalism, rationalist, rationalize, rationale.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 rational、rationally、rationalism、rationalist、rationalize、rationale。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the disciplines: bounded rationality, economic rationality, formal rationality, instrumental rationality.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出学科用法：有限理性、经济理性、形式理性、工具理性。

normal.en: rationality is the quality; rationalism is the doctrine; rationale is the stated reason.
normal.cn: rationality 是性质，rationalism 是学说，rationale 是给出的理由。

normal.en: A rational decision can still be wrong; rationality is about the process, not the outcome.
normal.cn: 理性的决定仍可能出错；rationality 讲的是过程，不是结果。

abstract.en: Picture a pair of scales that keeps tipping until each side holds the same weight of evidence.
abstract.cn: 想象一架天平不断倾斜，直到两边承载的证据重量相等。

abstract.en: Picture a ledger where every claim must be entered with its receipt.
abstract.cn: 想象一本账簿，每一条主张都必须附上收据才能入账。

abstract.en: Picture a machine that computes the shortest route but never asks whether the destination matters.
abstract.cn: 想象一台只计算最短路线、却从不问目的地是否重要的机器。

examples.en: The study tested the rationality of consumers' choices under time pressure.
examples.cn: 该研究检验了消费者在时间压力下选择的合理性。

examples.en: Bounded rationality does not abandon reason; it places reason inside real constraints.
examples.cn: 有限理性并未放弃理性，而是把理性放进真实约束之中。

examples.en: A purely instrumental rationality may be efficient and still aim at the wrong end.
examples.cn: 纯粹的工具理性可以很高效，却仍可能指向错误的目的。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「ratio（比例）算得清」——凡事按比例、按账目核算 → rationality 理性、合理性

root: 拉丁 ratio「计算、账目、理性」→ rationalis「理性的」→ 晚期拉丁 rationalitas；英语 rationality。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses circle one idea: ratio is reckoning, and rationality is the quality of being reckonable, defensible, or efficiently calculated — in a mind, an argument, an economy or an institution.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项围绕一个观念：ratio 是核算，rationality 则是可核算、可辩护或可高效计算的性质——它可落在心智、论证、经济或制度上。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a scale held level by equal weights of evidence.
core.cn: 核心意象：两边证据等重而保持水平的天平。

branches.en: MIND AND ARGUMENT: the faculty of reckoning, and the consistency of what it produces.
branches.cn: 心智与论证：核算能力，以及其产物的前后一致。

branches.en: CALCULATED CHOICE: economics turns reckoning into preference-maximizing selection.
branches.cn: 计算性选择：经济学把核算变成偏好最大化选择。

branches.en: LIMITS: the same choice, bounded by time and incomplete information.
branches.cn: 限度：同一种选择，被时间与不完整信息所限。

branches.en: ACCOUNTABILITY: reasons must be given, whether to a philosopher or to an institution.
branches.cn: 可交代性：无论面对哲学家还是制度，都必须给出理由。

branches.en: MACHINERY: rules can become rigid, and calculation can detach from the worth of its goal.
branches.cn: 机械性：规则会僵化，计算也会与目标的价值脱钩。

intro.en: Rationality is an adjective turned into a quality noun: Latin ratio, the adjective suffix -alis, then the abstract suffix -itas, carried into English as -ity.
intro.cn: rationality 是形容词转为性质名词：拉丁 ratio，加形容词后缀 -alis，再加抽象后缀 -itas，以英语 -ity 形式传入。

latinIntro.en: The ratio family includes ratio, rational, rationality, rationale, rationalize, ration and rate, all centred on counting and reckoning; ratio also gave the mathematical word ratio.
latinIntro.cn: ratio 词族包括 ratio、rational、rationality、rationale、rationalize、ration、rate，核心都在计数与核算；ratio 也直接成为数学里的「比」。

items.meaning: the quality of being guided by reason
items.example: The panel questioned the rationality of the pricing rule.
items.exampleCN: 专家组质疑该定价规则的合理性。

items.example: She gave a rational explanation for the delay.
items.exampleCN: 她对延误给出了合理的解释。
他理性地权衡了两份报价。

items.meaning: the view that reason is the chief source of knowledge
items.meaningCN: 认为理性是知识主要来源的学说
items.exampleCN: 理性主义与纯粹经验主义相对。

items.meaning: to organize on rational lines; to justify after the fact
items.meaningCN: 按理性重组；事后找理由
items.example: The firm rationalized its supply chain.
items.exampleCN: 该公司对供应链进行了合理化重组。

items.meaning: the stated set of reasons for something
items.meaningCN: 某事物明示的理由体系
items.example: The report explains the rationale for the new fee.
items.exampleCN: 报告解释了收取新费用的理由。

items.example: The ratio of students to teachers is ten to one.

items.meaning: the quality of being contrary to reason
items.example: The model allows for moments of irrationality.
items.exampleCN: 该模型容许非理性的时刻存在。

definition_zh: 缠绕；交织；使紧密相连
definition_en: to twist or wind things together so that they form one strand
core_image: 两股麻绳在指尖被拧成一股，再也分不出哪根是哪根
scene: 两家人因一场婚事结为一体，此后命运再也分不开。 Two families became entwined through a single marriage.
sceneCN: 这里 entwine 是「交织；紧密相连」（第 2 个义项：抽象事物彼此缠绕）；句意：一场婚事把两个家族缠绕在一起。

senses.title: To twist strands into one
senses.definition: to wind two or more threads or wires around each other
senses.definitionCN: 把两根以上的线或丝互相绕紧
senses.example: The craftsperson entwines hemp and silk.
senses.exampleCN: 工匠把麻线与丝线捻在一起。
senses.why: The stem names twisting twice over, so the verb describes strands that lose their separate identity.
senses.whyCN: 词干本义是拧上两遍，因此动词描述失去各自动独立形态的线股。

senses.title: To link lives or ideas closely
senses.definition: to connect people, events, or themes so that they cannot be separated
senses.definitionCN: 把人、事件或主题连接得无法分开
senses.example: Trade entwined the two port cities.
senses.exampleCN: 贸易把两座港口城市连在一起。
senses.why: Applied to abstractions, the physical twisting becomes a relation of mutual dependence.
senses.whyCN: 用于抽象事物时，实体的拧转变成相互依存的关系。

senses.title: To encircle with something twined
senses.definition: to surround or decorate by winding something around a body or object
senses.definitionCN: 通过绕缠某物来包围或装饰身体或器物
senses.example: Climbers entwined the trunk with rope.
senses.exampleCN: 攀爬者用绳索绕住树干。
senses.why: Here the object of winding is external, so the verb means to wrap rather than to merge.
senses.whyCN: 此时被缠绕的是外物，因此动词指包绕而非合一。

intro.en: Entwine pairs the prefix en- with twine, a native word for a strand twisted twice.
intro.cn: entwine 由前缀 en- 加本族词 twine 构成，twine 指拧了两次的线股。

items.en: A root meaning two produced words for doubling.
items.cn: 表二义的词根产出众多双义派生词。

items.en: Twinum named a thread twisted double.
items.cn: twinum 指双股拧成的线。

items.en: Twine becomes both noun and verb in craft use.
items.cn: 中古英语 twine 在工艺语境兼作名词与动词。

items.en: Entwine is attested in poetry and rope work.
items.cn: 近代早期 entwine 见于诗歌与绳艺记录。

items.en: The word feels literary, common in descriptions of plants and fates.
items.cn: 现代英语中该词带文学色彩，常用于植物与命运描写。

note.en: Group one holds the twine family and rhyming builds; group two holds other verbs of joining.
note.cn: 第一组是 twine 同族与同尾词；第二组是其他表示连合的动词。

entries.definition: The noun and verb of twisting, which supplies the stem.
entries.definitionCN: 表拧转的名词与动词，提供词干。

entries.definition: Adds inter-, stressing that both sides twist into each other.
entries.definitionCN: 加 inter-，强调双方互绕。

entries.definition: Frequent as an adjective of hands, hair, and histories.
entries.definitionCN: 常作形容词，修饰手、发与历史。

entries.definition: Built on wind rather than twine, and rarer still.
entries.definitionCN: 以 wind 为词干，比 entwine 更生僻。

entries.definition: To twist into a snarl; the result is trouble rather than unity.
entries.definitionCN: 乱绕成结，结果是麻烦而非一体。

entries.definition: To pass strands alternately, common in metalwork and design.
entries.definitionCN: 线股交替穿过，常见于金工与设计。

entries.definition: To make fabric by crossing threads at right angles.
entries.definitionCN: 以垂直交织成织物。

entries.definition: To weave three or more strands into a patterned length.
entries.definitionCN: 把三股以上编成有花纹的一束。

normalIntro.en: En plus twine: to put things into the state of a doubled strand.
normalIntro.cn: en 加 twine：使事物变成双股合一线的状态。

normal.en: Two or more strands are needed; one cannot entwine alone.
normal.cn: 需要两股以上，单股无法 entwine。

normal.en: Literary style prefers entwine where everyday speech says mix.
normal.cn: 文学语体用 entwine，日常说 mix。

normal.en: Entwined fingers is a stock image of intimacy.
normal.cn: 十指交扣是表现亲密的固定意象。

normal.en: Use with passive for plants: the gate was entwined with roses.
normal.cn: 写植物时常用被动：大门被玫瑰缠绕。

normal.en: Do not swap with entangle, which implies a mess.
normal.cn: 不要与 entangle 互换，后者含混乱之意。

abstract.en: Picture two ropes becoming a single thicker rope.
abstract.cn: 想象两根绳拧成一根更粗的绳。

abstract.en: Imagine ivy climbing a doorframe in slow spirals.
abstract.cn: 想象常春藤沿门框缓缓盘旋而上。

abstract.en: Think of two family trees whose branches grow into each other.
abstract.cn: 想想两棵家谱树的枝杈相互长在一起。

examples.en: She entwined the two cables for extra strength.
examples.cn: 她把两股电缆绞在一起以增加强度。

examples.en: Their fortunes were entwined by one contract.
examples.cn: 一纸合同把他们的命运绑在一起。

examples.en: Ivy entwines the old wall each summer.
examples.cn: 每年夏天常春藤都会缠上那堵旧墙。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「因双拧」——因为两股一起拧，所以 entwine 是缠绕交织；这只是拆词联想，与词源无关。

root: 原始日耳曼语表二义词根 → 古英语 twinum（双股线）→ 中古英语 twine＋en- → entwine，核心义「拧成一股」。

sensesIntro.en: The verb starts with rope work, moves to binding lives together, and ends with wrapping around an object.
sensesIntro.cn: 这个动词起于绳索工艺，转向把命运绑定，最后指环绕某物。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: separate strands losing their edges as they are twisted together.
core.cn: 核心意象：各股线在拧转中失去彼此边界。

branches.en: Craft work supplies the literal base sense.
branches.cn: 工艺操作提供本义基础。

branches.en: Abstraction turns twisting into interdependence.
branches.cn: 抽象化把拧转变为相互依存。

branches.en: Wrapping keeps the strands distinct but enclosing.
branches.cn: 包绕让线股仍分明却形成围合。

branches.en: Both describe hands working with cord.
branches.cn: 两者都描述双手与绳线作业。

branches.en: Marriages and ivy both enclose what they touch.
branches.cn: 婚姻与藤蔓都会围住所接触之物。

intro.en: A native prefix and a native stem produce a family that stays mostly English.
intro.cn: 本族前缀配本族词干，词族基本保持英语本色。

latinIntro.en: Latin Du_o and plicare supplied learned rivals such as duplicate and plait.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 duo 与 plicare 提供了 duplicate 与 plait 之类的书面竞争词。

items.exampleCN: twice 保留同一数字概念。

items.example: The form works as an adjective.

definition_zh: n. 国会议员（尤指美国众议员）
definition_en: a man who is a member of a national congress, especially in the United States
core_image: 一位胸前别着徽章、在议事厅起身发言的人
scene: 这位议员投票反对该法案。 The congressman voted against the bill.
sceneCN: 第 1 个义项：congressman 指国会议员；句意是这位议员投票反对该法案。

senses.title: A member of the US House

senses.definitionCN: 美国众议院的成员
senses.example: The congressman voted against the bill.
senses.exampleCN: 这位议员投票反对该法案。
senses.why: The word joins congress and man.
senses.whyCN: 该词由 congress 与 man 合成。

senses.title: A member of a congress

senses.definitionCN: 国家立法机构的成员
senses.example: The congressman spoke for his province.
senses.exampleCN: 这位议员为本省发声。
senses.why: The wider sense travels beyond America.
senses.whyCN: 较宽的义项超出美国范围。

intro.en: Congressman is congress plus man, one who sits in the congress.
intro.cn: congressman 是 congress 加 man，即坐在国会里的人。

items.en: Congressus means a coming together.
items.cn: congressus 意为聚到一起。

items.en: Congress named an assembly.
items.cn: 十七世纪 congress 指集会。

items.en: It named the national legislature.
items.cn: 十八世纪指国家立法机构。

items.en: Congressman named its member.
items.cn: 十八世纪 congressman 指其成员。

entries.definition: The national law-making assembly.
entries.definitionCN: 国家立法机构。

entries.definition: Relating to the congress.

entries.definition: A woman member of congress.

entries.definition: A member of a senate.

entries.definition: A person who makes laws.
entries.definitionCN: 立法者。

entries.definitionCN: 经选举代表他人的人。

entries.definition: A person who writes legislation.
entries.definitionCN: 制定法律的人。

normalIntro.en: A congressman is one man inside the congress.
normalIntro.cn: congressman 就是国会里的一个人。

normal.en: Congressus means a gathering.

abstract.en: One raised hand in a full hall.

examples.cn: 这位议员在本选区会见农民。

sensesIntro.en: One seat in a national assembly, usually the American one.
sensesIntro.cn: 国家议事机构中的一个席位，通常指美国。

core.cn: 核心意象：议事厅里起身发言的一位西装身影

branches.cn: 对法案投下的反对票。

branches.en: A district office and its staff.

branches.en: A speech for a whole province.

definition_zh: 公然的；明目张胆的；刺眼的；喧哗刺耳的
definition_en: done openly and unashamedly, or offensively conspicuous
core_image: 考试时把课本摊在桌上抄的人
scene: 监考老师转身的一瞬，他把答案摊得明明白白。 It was a blatant attempt to buy votes.
sceneCN: 这里 blatant 是「公然的、明目张胆的」（第 1 个义项：毫不掩饰地做出可耻之事）；句意是这是一次明目张胆的买票企图。

pos.zh: 公然的；明目张胆的；刺眼的

derivatives.zh: blatant 加 -ly，义为「公然地；赤裸裸地」

senses.title: Openly shameless in wrongdoing
senses.definition: doing something bad openly, without trying to hide it
senses.definitionCN: 公然做坏事，不加掩饰
senses.example: It was a blatant attempt to buy votes.
senses.exampleCN: 这是一次明目张胆的买票企图。
senses.why: The old sense of loud coarse noise shifted to loud, coarse behaviour.
senses.whyCN: 旧义「喧闹粗哑之声」转移到「喧闹粗鄙之行」。

senses.title: Offensively conspicuous
senses.definition: so obvious and loud that it offends the eye or mind
senses.definitionCN: 过于显眼张扬以致令人反感
senses.example: The blatant logo covered the whole jacket.
senses.exampleCN: 那枚巨大的商标铺满了整件外套。
senses.why: What shouts at the senses earns the name of the shouting word.
senses.whyCN: 向感官叫嚷之物便承袭了「叫嚷」之词。

senses.title: Of lies, utterly obvious
senses.definition: of a lie or falsehood, so bare that no one can miss it
senses.definitionCN: 谎言赤裸到无人可以忽视
senses.example: His excuse was a blatant lie from start to finish.
senses.exampleCN: 他的借口从头到尾都是明摆着的谎话。
senses.why: A lie too loud to hide is described with the loudness word.
senses.whyCN: 响亮到藏不住的谎言，便以「响亮」之词形容。

senses.title: Showing total disregard
senses.definition: expressing complete indifference to rules or feelings
senses.definitionCN: 对规则或他人感受表现出全然的漠视
senses.example: The factory showed blatant disregard for safety rules.
senses.exampleCN: 这家工厂对安全规章全然不顾。
senses.why: Ignoring rules loudly is a form of noisiness toward society.
senses.whyCN: 大张旗鼓地无视规则，是对社会的一种「喧哗」。

senses.title: Of advertising, crudely direct
senses.definition: of promotion, crudely direct and without subtlety
senses.definitionCN: 推销方式生硬直接、毫无含蓄
senses.example: The film was spoiled by blatant product placement.
senses.exampleCN: 赤裸裸的植入广告毁了这部电影。
senses.why: Sales talk that shouts has the same coarse loudness as the old sense.
senses.whyCN: 叫卖式的推销与旧义的粗响一脉相承。

senses.title: Of manner, aggressively forward
senses.definition: of behaviour, pushy and aggressive in a way that jars
senses.definitionCN: 举止咄咄逼人、令人不适
senses.example: Her blatant self-promotion annoyed the whole team.
senses.exampleCN: 她张扬的自我推销惹恼了整个团队。
senses.why: Pushiness is noise made with the body instead of the voice.
senses.whyCN: 张扬是身体代替喉咙发出的噪音。

senses.title: Of colour or design, glaring
senses.definition: of colour or style, glaring and lacking taste
senses.definitionCN: 色彩或风格俗艳刺目、缺乏品位
senses.example: Blatant wallpaper made the room unbearable.
senses.exampleCN: 艳俗的墙纸让房间令人难以忍受。
senses.why: Loud colours literally make visual noise.
senses.whyCN: 扎眼的色彩正是视觉上的「噪音」。

senses.title: Of sounds, coarse and noisy (older use)
senses.definition: of sound, loud, harsh, and coarse, the original sense
senses.definitionCN: 声音响亮粗厉，为该词本义
senses.example: The blatant horns announced the procession.
senses.exampleCN: 粗亮的号角宣告了队伍的到来。
senses.why: Coined for loud flapping or quacking noise before any moral sense existed.
senses.whyCN: 该词最初即为形容粗厉声响而造，后才生出道德义。

intro.en: Blatant was coined by Edmund Spenser for loud, coarse noise.
intro.cn: blatant 由斯宾塞所创，本指粗厉喧闹之声。

items.en: Edmund Spenser coined blatant in The Faerie Queene for a blatant beast with a thousand tongues, a figure of slander.
items.cn: 1596 年斯宾塞在《仙后》中创造 blatant，形容「千舌诽谤兽」的喧噪。

items.en: probably imitative, echoing Latin blatire, to gossip or babble.
items.cn: 一般认为系拟声造词，或受拉丁语 blatire「喋喋闲聊」影响。

items.en: in 17th-century Scots it meant filthy or loose in morals.
items.cn: 17 世纪苏格兰用法中指品行污秽放荡。

items.en: the sound sense faded as the sense of offensively obvious wrongdoing grew.
items.cn: 17 至 19 世纪间，声音义渐衰，「扎眼的公然冒犯」义渐盛。

items.en: now standard for anything shamelessly obvious.
items.cn: 今为标准词，泛指一切无耻的明目张胆。

note.en: Blatant has no common relatives; look-alikes sound similar, and near-meanings gather shameless-obvious words.
note.cn: blatant 无常见同族词；形近组收音近词，近义组收无耻外露类词。

definition_zh: 祝福；祝祷；（礼拜结束时的）祝福祈祷
definition_en: a spoken blessing, especially one asking for God's favour and protection
core_image: 礼拜结束时牧师张开双手、向着人群说出的祝祷词
scene: 礼拜结束，众人低头，牧师张开双手诵出祝词。 The priest raised his hands and gave the crowd his benediction.
sceneCN: 这里 benediction 是「祝福、祝祷」（第 1 个义项：正式说出的祝福语）；句意是牧师举手为人群祝福。

senses.title: A spoken blessing asking for divine favour
senses.definition: words asking for God's help and protection, said especially at the end of a service
senses.definitionCN: 祈求上帝护佑的话语，常见于礼拜结束时
senses.example: The priest raised his hands and gave the crowd his benediction.
senses.exampleCN: 牧师举起双手，为人群致祝祷。
senses.why: Bene means well and dicere means to speak, so it is good speech over people.
senses.whyCN: bene 意为「好」，dicere 意为「说」，合起来即「说吉利话于人身」。

senses.title: A happy event felt as a blessing
senses.definition: something that brings happiness or relief, as if sent from above
senses.definitionCN: 带来幸福或解脱的事，仿佛上天的恩赐
senses.example: The cool rain after the drought was a benediction on the fields.
senses.exampleCN: 旱后的凉雨落在田里，如同天赐之福。
senses.why: The good-speaking image widens to any goodness that seems heaven-sent.
senses.whyCN: 「说好话赐福」的意象扩大为一切像上天所赐的好处。

intro.en: Benediction is Latin bene, well, plus dicere, to speak.
intro.cn: benediction 由拉丁语 bene「好」加 dicere「说」构成。

items.en: the root deik- meant to point out, to pronounce.

items.en: benedictio meant a speaking well of, a blessing.
items.cn: 拉丁语 benedictio 意为「说好话、祝福」。

items.en: benedicoun passed the word into medieval French usage.
items.cn: 古法语 benedicoun 使该词进入中世纪法语。

items.en: English borrowed benediction for church blessings.
items.cn: 十五世纪英语借入 benediction，用于教会祝福礼。

items.en: it also names figurative blessings in daily life.
items.cn: 如今也用于比喻日常生活中的福气。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the bene- root or dict- root; the near-meaning group gathers blessing words.

definition_en: to make someone confused, or to muddle something completely
core_image: 说明书绕来绕去，读者越看越晕
scene: 攒了一下午家具，说明书却让他一头雾水。 The confusing instructions befuddled him completely.

senses.title: To confuse the mind
senses.definition: to make a person unable to think clearly
senses.definitionCN: 使人无法清晰思考

senses.exampleCN: 费解的说明书让他彻底晕头转向。

senses.title: To muddle with drink

intro.en: Befuddle adds the be- prefix to fuddle, an old drinking word.
intro.cn: befuddle 在古老的酒词 fuddle 前加 be- 前缀。

items.en: fuddle appeared in the sixteenth century, probably Low German, meaning to get tipsy; its deeper origin is uncertain.
items.cn: fuddle 十六世纪出现，一般认为来自低地德语，意为「微醺」，更早来源不确定。

items.en: fuddle meant to make drunk.
items.cn: 十六至十七世纪 fuddle 意为「使醉」。

items.en: befuddle was formed as an intensified verb.
items.cn: 十八世纪强化动词 befuddle 构成。

items.en: the meaning widened from drink to any confusion.
items.cn: 十九世纪词义由酒扩展到一切困惑。

items.en: befuddled is now the usual form, for drink, fatigue, or jargon.
items.cn: 如今 befuddled 常用于形容醉酒、疲惫或术语造成的昏乱。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the be- prefix or the fuddle root; the near-meaning group gathers confusing words.
