intro.cn: befuddle 在 fuddle 上叠 be-，把「昏乱」再加一层。

latinIntro.en: There is no Latin base; fuddle is Germanic, probably Low German.
latinIntro.cn: 这里没有拉丁词基，fuddle 属日耳曼语源，一般认为出自低地德语。

derivatives.zh: 基础词，义为「使醉；使混乱」
由过去分词转形容词，义为「糊涂的；昏乱的」

definition_zh: adj. 破坏的；破坏性的；毁灭的；（对己）自毁的
definition_en: causing great damage to things, people or relationships, or likely to harm the person doing it
core_image: 一面墙被推倒，砖块散在脚下；一段关系里，每次开口都留下裂痕
scene: 批评可以是破坏性的。 Criticism can be destructive.
sceneCN: 第 1 个义项：destructive 指破坏性的；句意是批评可以是破坏性的。

pos.zh: 破坏的；破坏性的；毁灭的

senses.title: Causing physical damage
senses.definition: causing great damage to things or places
senses.definitionCN: 对物品或地方造成严重损坏
senses.example: The storm was destructive along the coast.
senses.exampleCN: 这场风暴在沿海一带破坏力极大。
senses.why: A wall pushed over with bricks at your feet.
senses.whyCN: 一面被推倒的墙，砖块散在脚下。

senses.title: Harming people or feelings
senses.definition: causing harm to a person, a relationship or confidence
senses.definitionCN: 对人、关系或信心造成伤害
senses.example: Destructive criticism leaves nothing to build on.
senses.exampleCN: 破坏性批评让人无从改进。
senses.why: A crack widening in a shared wall.
senses.whyCN: 共用墙上一道不断变宽的裂缝。

senses.title: Tending to harm oneself
senses.definition: likely to harm the person or thing doing it
senses.definitionCN: 可能伤害行为者自身的
senses.example: The habit became self-destructive.
senses.exampleCN: 这个习惯变成了自我毁灭。
senses.why: A fire burning its own fuel supply.
senses.whyCN: 一场烧掉自身燃料的火。

intro.en: Destructive comes from Latin destructivus, from destruere, de- down plus struere to build, so literally to unbuild what was built.
intro.cn: destructive 源自拉丁语 destructivus，来自 destruere，由 de-（向下）加 struere（建造）构成，字面就是「拆掉建好的东西」。

items.en: Struere meant to build or pile up.
items.cn: struere 意为建造、堆起。

items.en: Destruere meant to pull down what was built.
items.cn: destruere 意为拆掉建好的东西。

items.en: Destructivus meant tending to pull down.
items.cn: destructivus 意为倾向于拆毁的。

items.en: Destructive entered English for causing ruin.
items.cn: 十五世纪 destructive 以造成毁坏义进入英语。

items.en: It widened to harm to feelings and habits.
items.cn: 十九世纪扩展到对感情与习惯的伤害。

items.en: Self-destructive now describes harmful behaviour.
items.cn: 如今 self-destructive 用来描述自毁行为。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the struct- build family; the near-meaning group names other ways of causing harm.
note.cn: 形近组共享 struct-（建造）家族；近义组是其他表示「造成伤害」的词。

entries.definition: The act of building; it shares struere but puts things up instead of pulling them down.
entries.definitionCN: 建造的行为；共享 struere，但是立起来而非拆下去。

entries.definition: Teaching or an order; it shares the struct- stem but concerns knowledge.
entries.definitionCN: 教学或指令；共享 struct- 词干，但关乎知识。

entries.definition: The act of destroying something.
entries.definitionCN: 摧毁某物的行为。

entries.definition: Having a bad effect on something.
entries.definitionCN: 对某事物有不良影响。

entries.definition: Likely to cause damage or injury.
entries.definitionCN: 可能造成损害或伤害。

entries.definition: Causing very great damage or shock.
entries.definitionCN: 造成极大破坏或震惊。

normalIntro.en: Destructive is de- down plus struct- build plus -ive tending to: tending to pull down what was built.
normalIntro.cn: destructive 就是 de-（向下）加 struct-（建造）加 -ive（倾向于）：倾向于把建好的东西拆下来。

normal.en: Struct- means build, as in structure.
normal.cn: struct- 意为建造，如 structure。

normal.en: De- turns building into unbuilding.
normal.cn: de- 把建造变成拆毁。

normal.en: -ive means tending to.
normal.cn: -ive 表示倾向于。

normal.en: Destructive criticism only tears down.
normal.cn: destructive criticism 只会拆台。

normal.en: Self-destructive harms the doer.
normal.cn: self-destructive 伤害的是行为者自己。

abstract.en: A wall pushed over with bricks at your feet.
abstract.cn: 一面被推倒的墙，砖块散在脚下。

abstract.en: A crack widening in a shared wall.
abstract.cn: 共用墙上一道不断变宽的裂缝。

abstract.en: A fire burning its own fuel supply.
abstract.cn: 一场烧掉自身燃料的火。

examples.en: The flood was highly destructive.
examples.cn: 这场洪水破坏性极强。

examples.en: Such remarks are destructive to a team.
examples.cn: 这类言论对团队有破坏性。

examples.en: They studied the destructive power of the quake.
examples.cn: 他们研究了这次地震的破坏力。

dict_mnemonic.text: destructive ＝ de（向下）＋ struct（建造，与 structure 同根拉丁语 struere）＋ -ive（倾向于…的）＝倾向于把建好的东西拆下去，「破坏性的」。

root: 拉丁语 struere（建造）→ de-＋struere → destruere（拆毁）→ destructivus → 英语 destructive

sensesIntro.en: One thing pulled down: a wall, a shared confidence and a person own habit.
sensesIntro.cn: 同一件被拆掉的东西：一面墙、一份共同的信心与一个人自己的习惯。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a wall pushed over with bricks scattered at your feet
core.cn: 核心意象：一面墙被推倒，砖块散在脚下

branches.en: A wall pushed over with bricks at your feet.
branches.cn: 一面被推倒的墙，砖块散在脚下。

branches.en: A crack widening in a shared wall.
branches.cn: 共用墙上一道不断变宽的裂缝。

branches.en: A fire burning its own fuel supply.
branches.cn: 一场烧掉自身燃料的火。

branches.en: Both leave something worse than before.
branches.cn: 两者都让事物比从前更糟。

branches.en: Both damage what cannot easily be rebuilt.
branches.cn: 两者都损坏难以重建的东西。

intro.en: Destructive is de- plus struct- plus -ive; the build root also raises construct and instruct.
intro.cn: destructive 由 de- 加 struct- 加 -ive 构成；建造这个词根也立起 construct 与 instruct。

latinIntro.en: Latin struere means to build, structura a fitting together and vastus empty or waste.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 struere 意为建造，structura 意为拼接，vastus 意为空旷荒芜。

definition_zh: 放弃（权利、要求）；克制（欲望）；否认
definition_en: to give up or deny oneself a right, claim, or desire
core_image: 把到手的果子从掌心推出去
scene: 遗产分割那天，她第一个签了字。 He chose to abnegate his share of the inheritance for the family's sake.
sceneCN: 这里 abnegate 是「放弃」（第 1 个义项：让出应得的权利）；句意为为了家人，他选择放弃自己那份遗产。

pos.zh: 克制、舍弃（自身欲望）；否认

derivatives.zh: 由动词加名词后缀 -ion 构成，义为「克制；自我舍弃」
合成名词，义为「自我克制；忘我」

senses.title: To give up a right or claim
senses.definition: to formally give up a right, claim, or privilege
senses.definitionCN: 正式放弃权利、主张或特权
senses.example: The minister abnegated any claim to the disputed land.
senses.exampleCN: 部长放弃了对争议土地的一切主张。
senses.why: The Latin negare means to deny; abnegating a claim is saying no to what was yours.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 negare 意为否认；放弃主张就是对原本属于你的东西说「不」。

senses.title: To deny oneself desires
senses.definition: to refuse oneself pleasures or comforts, usually from principle
senses.definitionCN: 出于原则而拒绝给自己享受或安逸
senses.example: Monastic rules require monks to abnegate ordinary comforts.
senses.exampleCN: 修道会规要求修士舍弃寻常的舒适。
senses.why: Saying no turns inward: the same denial is applied to one's own wants.
senses.whyCN: 「说不」转向内部：同样的否定用在自身欲望上。

senses.title: To deny or disown a thing
senses.definition: to declare something untrue or refuse to acknowledge it
senses.definitionCN: 宣称某事不实或拒绝承认
senses.example: The board abnegated the rumours about merger plans.
senses.exampleCN: 董事会否认了有关合并计划的传闻。
senses.why: Denial is the verb root itself; pushing a statement away is the outermost use of the word.
senses.whyCN: 否认正是词根本义；把一个说法推开，是这个词最外层的用法。

intro.en: Abnegate joins Latin negare, to deny, with the away-prefix; saying no and pushing away at once.
intro.cn: abnegate 把拉丁语 negare「否认」与离开前缀结合：既说不，又推开。

items.en: A root for saying no, ne- plus a verbal ending, is reconstructed.
items.cn: 表示「说不」的词根 ne- 加动词词尾，属重构形式。

items.en: Negare meant to deny or refuse.
items.cn: 拉丁语 negare 意为否认、拒绝。

items.en: Abnegare meant to refuse something away from oneself, to renounce.
items.cn: 晚期拉丁语 abnegare 意为拒之于己外、弃绝。

items.en: Abnegate entered learned English, mostly religious in tone.
items.cn: 十七世纪 abnegate 进入学术英语，多带宗教色彩。

items.en: The noun abnegation is now more common than the verb.
items.cn: 如今名词 abnegation 比动词更常用。

note.en: Abnegate belongs to the neg- deny family and is often met as the noun abnegation.
note.cn: abnegate 属于 neg-「否认」词族，更常见的形态是名词 abnegation。

entries.definition: self-denial or renunciation
entries.definitionCN: 名词形式，义为克制、自我舍弃

entries.definition: to nullify or deny, without the away-prefix
entries.definitionCN: 否定、使无效；同根 negare 但无离开前缀

entries.definition: third-person form of the verb
entries.definitionCN: 动词三单形式

entries.definition: to give up formally
entries.definitionCN: 正式放弃；不带否认色彩

entries.definition: to give up a pleasure or advantage
entries.definitionCN: 放弃享受；语域更日常

entries.definition: the practice of refusing oneself pleasures
entries.definitionCN: 自我克制的做法；对应第 2 义项

normalIntro.en: Five anchors tie abnegate to the pushed-away fruit.
normalIntro.cn: 五个抓手把 abnegate 与被推开的果实绑在一起。

normal.en: ab- away + neg- deny: deny and push away.
normal.cn: ab-（离开）＋ neg-（否认）：既说不又推开。

normal.en: neg- family: negative, negate, neglect.
normal.cn: neg- 词族：negative、negate、neglect。

normal.en: abnegation of self: monastic word.
normal.cn: abnegation of self：修道用语。

normal.en: Abnegate rights: say no to your own claim.
normal.cn: abnegate rights：对自己的主张说不。

normal.en: The noun is commoner than the verb today.
normal.cn: 如今名词比动词常用。

abstract.en: Feel a ripe apple pushed across the table.
abstract.cn: 感到一只熟苹果被推过桌面。

abstract.en: Hear a firm no said to oneself.
abstract.cn: 听见对自己说出的坚定「不」。

abstract.en: See a door closed on a comfort.
abstract.cn: 看见一扇门对着安逸关上。

examples.en: He abnegated his claim to the family estate.
examples.cn: 他放弃了对家族产业的主张。

examples.en: The discipline required them to abnegate every luxury.
examples.cn: 戒律要求他们舍弃一切奢华。

examples.en: A life of abnegation shaped her plain habits.
examples.cn: 克己的生活塑造了她朴素的习惯。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「我不内给」——我对自己说：不内给，好东西先推出去

root: 拉丁语 abnegare「拒之于外」＝ ab-「离开」＋ negare「否认」（词根出自重构的原始印欧 ne-「不」）。经晚期拉丁语于十七世纪进入英语；名词 abnegation 常表「克己」。

sensesIntro.en: Three senses aim one no in three directions: at a claim, at a desire, at a statement.
sensesIntro.cn: 三个义项把同一个「不」指向三个方向：主张、欲望、说法。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a ripe fruit pushed off the palm.
core.cn: 核心意象：熟果被从掌心推开。

branches.en: THE CLAIM: outward rights are the first to be refused.
branches.cn: 主张：外在的权利首先被拒绝。

branches.en: THE DESIRE: the no turns inward on one's own wants.
branches.cn: 欲望：这个「不」转向自身欲望。

branches.en: THE STATEMENT: denial pushed furthest, at truth claims.
branches.cn: 说法：否认推得最远，指向真伪判断。

branches.en: GIVING UP: both senses are refusals of what one could have.
branches.cn: 舍弃：这两个义项都是对可得之物的拒绝。

branches.en: ONE NO: every sense is negare carrying the away-prefix.
branches.cn: 同一个「不」：每个义项都是带着离开前缀的 negare。

intro.en: A denial root with a leaving prefix; the family is easy to map.
intro.cn: 否认词根加离开前缀；词族脉络清晰。

latinIntro.en: Latin negare is classical; the Indo-European ne- particle is a reconstruction.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 negare 见于古典文献；印欧小品词 ne- 属重构。

items.example: It is the reconstructed ancestor of neg-.
items.exampleCN: 它是 neg- 的重构祖先。

derivatives.zh: 由动词加 -ion 构成，义为「克制；自我舍弃」
合成名词，义为「自我克制；忘我」

definition_zh: 纯语主义的；过分讲究语言纯正的；拘守正统的
definition_en: insisting on strict purity, especially in language or style
core_image: 一位编辑把口语逐字改回书面语，不肯让步
scene: 编辑一遍遍把口语改回书面语，这种纯语主义的坚持让稿子失去了活气。 The editor kept restoring the formal phrasing, a puristic refusal to accept how people actually spoke.
sceneCN: 这里 puristic 指纯语主义的（第 1 个义项：语言纯化）；句意为编辑一遍遍把口语改回书面语，这种坚持让稿子失去了活气。

pos.zh: 纯语主义的；过分讲究纯正的

senses.title: Puristic language
senses.definition: insisting that a language has one correct form and should be kept free of foreign or colloquial elements
senses.definitionCN: 坚持一种语言只有一种正确形式，并应剔除外来成分与口语成分
senses.example: The editor kept restoring the formal phrasing, a puristic refusal to accept how people actually spoke.
senses.exampleCN: 编辑一遍遍把口语改回书面语，这是纯语主义地拒绝接受人们实际的说法。
senses.why: The target here is usage: the word judges an attitude to how a language is spoken, not just to its grammar.
senses.whyCN: 这里针对的是用法：这个词评判的是对「语言怎么说」的态度，而不只是语法。

senses.title: Puristic style
senses.definition: demanding an art or design stripped of mixed influences and ornament
senses.definitionCN: 要求艺术或设计剔除混合影响与装饰
senses.example: The building's puristic lines allowed no ornament at all.
senses.exampleCN: 这座建筑的纯语主义线条不允许任何装饰。
senses.why: Architecture and music borrow the word when purity becomes a programme rather than a preference.
senses.whyCN: 当纯粹变成一种纲领而不是一种偏好时，建筑与音乐就借用这个词。

senses.title: Puristic as a label
senses.definition: a critical label for someone who values correctness above communication
senses.definitionCN: 用来批评那些把正确性看得比沟通更重的人的标签
senses.example: Calling him puristic was a polite way of saying he was impossible to work with.
senses.exampleCN: 说他纯语主义，是礼貌地说他没法共事。
senses.why: In ordinary speech the adjective is usually a criticism in disguise, aimed at a person rather than a rule.
senses.whyCN: 在日常言语里，这个形容词通常是伪装起来的批评，指向人而不是规则。

intro.en: Puristic joins Latin purus, 'pure', to the English suffix -istic; the word is purity turned into a policy.
intro.cn: puristic 把拉丁语 purus（纯净）与英语后缀 -istic 结合；这个词是被变成政策的「纯粹」。

items.en: Purus meant clean, unmixed, free of foreign matter.
items.cn: purus 意为干净、未混杂、没有杂质。

items.en: Old French and English kept the word for what is unmixed.
items.cn: 古法语和英语保留了这个词，指未混杂之物。

items.en: Purism named the wish to keep a language or art unmixed.
items.cn: purism 指让语言或艺术保持不混杂的愿望。

items.en: Nineteenth-century critics applied it to language reform.
items.cn: 十九世纪的批评者把它用于语言改革。

items.en: Today it often accuses someone of valuing purity over use.
items.cn: 今天它常用来指责某人把纯粹看得比使用更重。

note.en: The look-alike group is the pur- family; the near-meaning group separates prescriptive, doctrinaire, fastidious and orthodox.
note.cn: 形近组是 pur 词族；近义组把「规定性的」「教条式的」「苛求的」「正统的」分开。

entries.definition: one who insists on purity.
entries.definitionCN: 坚持纯粹的人。

entries.definition: the doctrine of keeping a form pure.
entries.definitionCN: 保持形式纯粹的主张。

entries.definition: the state of being unmixed.
entries.definitionCN: 未混杂的状态。

entries.definition: a strict moral reformer.
entries.definitionCN: 严格的道德改革者。

entries.definition: laying down rules of correct use.
entries.definitionCN: 规定正确用法的。

entries.definition: rigidly applying a theory.
entries.definitionCN: 僵硬套用理论的。

entries.definition: hard to please about detail.
entries.definitionCN: 对细节难以满意的。

entries.definition: following the accepted standard.
entries.definitionCN: 遵循公认标准的。

normalIntro.en: The hooks keep the picture of an editor restoring every comma of a spoken sentence.
normalIntro.cn: 以下联想留住「编辑把一句口语的每个逗号都改回书面语」的画面。

normal.en: Puristic carries pure: the word is purity wearing a rulebook.
normal.cn: puristic 里有 pure：这个词是穿着规则手册的纯粹。

normal.en: Picture a manuscript with every contraction crossed out in red.
normal.cn: 想象一份稿子，每个缩略形式都被红笔划掉。

normal.en: Say pyoo-RIS-tik; the middle sounds like wrist, rigid and locked.
normal.cn: 读 pyoo-RIS-tik，中间像 wrist，僵硬而锁死。

normal.en: The ending -istic turns a belief into a manner of acting.
normal.cn: 词尾 -istic 把一种信念变成一种行事方式。

normal.en: Ask: is the rule protecting meaning, or protecting the rule?
normal.cn: 问一句：这条规则是在保护意义，还是在保护规则本身？

abstract.en: Puristic authority rests on the fear that a language will dissolve if it mixes.
abstract.cn: 纯语主义的权威建立在一种恐惧上：语言一混合就会溶解。

abstract.en: The word describes a border guard, not a grammarian.
abstract.cn: 这个词描述的是边检员，不是语法学家。

abstract.en: Every puristic rule is a claim about who owns a language.
abstract.cn: 每条纯语主义规则都是关于谁拥有这门语言的主张。

examples.en: The editor kept restoring the formal phrasing, a puristic refusal to accept how people actually spoke.
examples.cn: 编辑一遍遍把口语改回书面语，这是纯语主义地拒绝接受人们实际的说法。

examples.en: The committee's puristic rejection of loanwords made the manual hard to read.
examples.cn: 委员会对外来词的纯语主义拒绝让手册变得难读。

examples.en: A prescriptive grammar describes the standard; a puristic one guards its borders.
examples.cn: 规定性语法描述标准，纯语主义语法则守卫标准的边界。

dict_mnemonic.text: pure（纯）+ istic（主义化的）→ 把语言纯正当作信条的。

root: 拉丁语 purus（纯净）+ 英语后缀 -istic

sensesIntro.en: The three senses follow one demand for purity through language, through art and design, and through the label applied to a person.
sensesIntro.cn: 三个义项追着同一个「纯粹」要求：穿过语言，穿过艺术与设计，最后落在贴到人身上的那个标签。

core.en: AN EDITOR WITH A RED PEN
core.cn: 一位拿着红笔的编辑

branches.en: A language kept free of foreign and colloquial forms.
branches.cn: 被排除外来与口语形式的语言。

branches.en: The same demand moved into art and design.
branches.cn: 同一个要求被搬进艺术与设计。

branches.en: Purity turned into a programme rather than a taste.
branches.cn: 变成纲领而不是品味的纯粹。

branches.en: The word used as a reproach against a person.
branches.cn: 被用作对人的责难的这个词。

branches.en: A rule defended for its purity, and the person who defends it.
branches.cn: 被以纯粹之名捍卫的规则，以及捍卫它的人。

intro.en: The pur- family covers purity, purify, pure, purist and purism; puristic is the adjective that makes the demand sound like a method.
intro.cn: pur 词族包括 purity、purify、pure、purist、purism；puristic 是让这项要求听起来像方法的形容词。

latinIntro.en: Latin purus gives the root, -itas makes purity and -ificare makes purify; -istic adds the tone of doctrine.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 purus 提供词根，-itas 造出 purity，-ificare 造出 purify；-istic 加上教义的腔调。

items.exampleCN: 一个严格的纯语主义者。

definition_zh: 耕作的；人工栽培的；（人）有教养的；后天培养出来的
definition_en: (of land) prepared and used for crops; (of plants or organisms) grown under human control; (of a person, taste or skill) developed by deliberate training
core_image: 一块行距笔直的田，作物比野地里的同类更壮；田边站着一位举止从容、说话有分寸的人
scene: 田里的行距被绳子量得笔直，苗高一致，杂草清得干净，主人说话轻缓而有分寸。 The cultivated field yields more than the wild plot beside it.
sceneCN: 这里指「经人工耕作与照管的」（第 1 个义项：耕地）；句意为这块耕作过的田比旁边的荒地收成更多。

pos.zh: 耕作的；人工栽培的；有教养的；后天培养的

derivatives.zh: cultivate + -ation（动作或结果）→ 耕作；培养
cultivate + -or（施动者或工具）→ 耕作的人；中耕机
cultivate + -ar（园艺名词后缀）→ 栽培品种
un-（否定）+ cultivated → 未开垦的；未受教育的
re-（重新）+ cultivated → 休耕后重新耕作的

senses.title: Land that has been tilled
senses.definition: describing land that has been broken, worked and used for crops rather than left wild
senses.definitionCN: 描述经过翻耕、整治并用于种植作物、而非任其荒芜的土地
senses.example: Cultivated land stops where the slope becomes too steep.
senses.exampleCN: 耕地到坡度过陡处为止。
senses.why: The past participle of cultivate turns the action into a state, so land carries the mark of having been worked.
senses.whyCN: cultivate 的过去分词把动作转为状态，因此土地带着「已被耕作」的印记。

senses.title: Field crops grown on purpose
senses.titleCN: 有目的种植的田间作物
senses.definition: describing crops that people have planted and tended in fields, as opposed to wild plants
senses.definitionCN: 描述人们种在田里并加以照管的作物，与野生植物相对
senses.example: Cultivated wheat shatters less easily than its wild ancestor.
senses.exampleCN: 栽培小麦比其野生祖先更不易落粒。
senses.why: Once a plant depends on people for sowing and weeding, it is described by the participle of the care it receives.
senses.whyCN: 一旦植物依赖人播种与除草，就用它所受照管的分词来描述。

senses.title: Garden plants from chosen stock
senses.titleCN: 由选育种苗栽培的园艺植物
senses.definition: describing ornamental or fruit plants raised from selected stock in a garden or nursery
senses.definitionCN: 描述在园圃或苗圃中由选育种苗育成的观赏或果树植物
senses.example: The cultivated rose has lost the scent of the wild briar.
senses.exampleCN: 栽培玫瑰已失去野蔷薇的香气。
senses.why: Garden plants are the clearest case of human choice: the stock itself, not only the soil, has been selected.
senses.whyCN: 园艺植物是人类选择最清楚的例子：被选的不仅是土壤，还有种苗本身。

senses.title: Grown in a laboratory medium
senses.titleCN: 在实验室培养基中培养的
senses.definition: describing microorganisms or cells grown under controlled laboratory conditions
senses.definitionCN: 描述在受控实验室条件下培养的微生物或细胞
senses.example: Cultivated cells behave differently from cells taken straight from tissue.
senses.exampleCN: 培养细胞的行为与直接从组织取出的细胞不同。
senses.why: Laboratory growth is deliberate cultivation, so the participle marks anything raised in a dish rather than in a body.
senses.whyCN: 实验室培养是有意的培育，因此这个分词标记一切在培养皿而非体内长成的东西。

senses.title: A person polished by education
senses.titleCN: 受过教育而举止得体的人
senses.definition: describing a person whose manners, speech and judgment have been refined by education and good company
senses.definitionCN: 描述举止、言谈与判断经教育与良好交往而变得优雅的人
senses.example: He was a cultivated man who never raised his voice.
senses.exampleCN: 他是一位有教养的男士，从不提高嗓门。
senses.why: The agricultural metaphor turns social: a person, like a garden, can be tended into a better shape.
senses.whyCN: 农业比喻转向社会：人如园子，可以被照料成更好的形状。

senses.title: A taste acquired by exposure
senses.definition: describing an appreciation that has been learned through repeated exposure rather than possessed naturally
senses.definitionCN: 描述经反复接触而学会、而非天生拥有的鉴赏力
senses.example: Her cultivated taste for opera began with film scores.
senses.exampleCN: 她对歌剧的后天品味始于电影配乐。
senses.why: Taste is not planted in a person at birth; it is grown by exposure, which is why the participle fits.
senses.whyCN: 品味并非与生俱来，而是靠接触长成，因此适合用这个分词。

senses.title: A skill built by training
senses.definition: describing an ability developed through deliberate practice rather than given by nature
senses.definitionCN: 描述经刻意练习发展出来、而非天赋所赐的能力
senses.example: His cultivated voice carried across the hall without strain.
senses.exampleCN: 他训练有素的嗓音毫不费力地传遍大厅。
senses.why: The contrast with native gifts is the point: what is cultivated was not there to begin with.
senses.whyCN: 与天赋的对照正是要点：被培养出来的东西起初并不存在。

senses.title: A relationship kept up on purpose
senses.definition: describing a friendship or contact that is deliberately maintained over time
senses.definitionCN: 描述长期被有意维持的友谊或人脉
senses.example: Their cultivated ties survived two changes of government.
senses.exampleCN: 他们经营的关系挺过了两次政府更替。
senses.why: A tie that is kept up is literally cultivated, and the participle records the effort behind its survival.
senses.whyCN: 被维持的关系确实是「被栽培」的，这个分词记录了它存活背后的投入。

intro.en: Cultivated is the past participle of cultivate used as an adjective. The verb came from Medieval Latin cultivare, and the adjectival use is recorded from the sixteenth century, with the social sense following in the eighteenth. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: cultivated 是 cultivate 的过去分词作形容词。这个动词来自中世纪拉丁 cultivare，形容词用法在十六世纪已有记录，社会义则在十八世纪出现。年代均为约数。

items.en: Cultivare meant to till or tend; its past participle cultivatus supplied the form that English turned into an adjective.
items.cn: cultivare 意为耕作或照管；其过去分词 cultivatus 提供了英语转化为形容词的形式。

items.en: The first English adjectival uses describe land and plants that have been worked, keeping close to the participle's literal force.
items.cn: 最早的英语形容词用法描述被耕作过的土地与植物，贴近分词的字面力量。

items.en: Enlightenment writing applied the word to people, manners and taste, so a cultivated man became one whose mind had been tended.
items.cn: 启蒙时期的写作把这个词用于人、举止与品味，于是有教养的人成了心智受过照料的人。

items.en: Microbiology adopted the participle for organisms grown in a medium, giving the word a second technical life.
items.cn: 微生物学采用这个分词指在培养基中生长的生物，使这个词获得第二种技术生命。

items.en: Modern English keeps both readings side by side: cultivated land and a cultivated accent, one literal and one figurative.
items.cn: 现代英语把两种读法并置：耕作的田地与有教养的口音，一为字面，一为比喻。

items.en: Source uncertain (first date): dictionaries date the adjectival use only approximately, and the exact path from agricultural to social meaning is not documented in detail.
items.cn: 来源不确定（首见年代）：辞书对形容词用法的年代只有约数，从农业义到社会义的具体路径也缺乏详细记载。

note.en: Group one holds participles and adjectives from the same root that are easily swapped; group two holds adjectives for a polished or trained person or thing.
note.cn: 第一组是同出该词根、极易互换的分词与形容词；第二组是描述「被磨得精致、受过训练」的人或物的形容词。

entries.definition: From culture, not cultivate: it can mean refined in manners or grown in a medium, as in cultured pearls.
entries.definitionCN: 来自 culture 而非 cultivate：既可指举止优雅，也可指在培养基中生长，如养殖珍珠。

entries.definition: The plain opposite: land never worked, or a person without training; it denies the participle rather than naming a new quality.
entries.definitionCN: 直接的反义：从未耕作的土地，或未受训练的人；它否定该分词，而不命名新性质。

entries.definition: Able to be cultivated, whether or not it actually is; cultivated land has already been worked.
entries.definitionCN: 能够被耕作，无论实际是否已耕；而 cultivated 的土地已经耕过。

entries.definition: The noun for a way of life or a growth medium; it names the field, while cultivated describes what came out of it.
entries.definitionCN: 指生活方式或培养基的名词；它命名场域，而 cultivated 描述从中产生的结果。

entries.definition: Purified or made elegant by taking away what is coarse; cultivated stresses the care that grew the quality, refined stresses the removal of roughness.
entries.definitionCN: 通过去除粗劣部分而变得纯净或优雅；cultivated 强调培育出该品质的照料，refined 强调去除粗糙。

entries.definition: Having received formal instruction; cultivated is broader and includes manners and taste acquired outside school.
entries.definitionCN: 受过正式教育；cultivated 范围更广，包含在校外获得的举止与品味。

entries.definition: Made manageable by domestication; it applies to animals and wildness, not to land care or personal polish.
entries.definitionCN: 通过驯化而变得可控；适用于动物与野性，不用于土地照料或个人修养。

entries.definition: Carefully prepared for a particular role or appearance; cultivated can be wider and less career-directed.
entries.definitionCN: 为特定角色或外表精心准备；cultivated 可以更宽，未必指向职业。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real fixed phrases and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: cultivate plus -ed: the action is finished, and what remains is a state.
normal.cn: cultivate 加 -ed：动作已完成，留下的是状态。

normal.en: The family runs cultivate, cultivation, cultivator, cultivable, cultivar, cultivated.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 cultivate、cultivation、cultivator、cultivable、cultivar、cultivated。

normal.en: Fixed phrases split the senses: cultivated land, cultivated plants, a cultivated man.
normal.cn: 固定搭配区分义项：耕地、栽培植物、有教养的人。

normal.en: The laboratory says cultivated cells; the garden says cultivated roses.
normal.cn: 实验室说培养细胞，园子说栽培玫瑰。

normal.en: The contrast is always with wild, native or untrained.
normal.cn: 它的对照项总是野生、天生或未受训练。

abstract.en: Picture a field whose straight rows are themselves a record of years of decisions.
abstract.cn: 想象一块田，笔直的行距本身就是多年决断的记录。

abstract.en: Picture a voice that has been sanded smooth by decades of practice.
abstract.cn: 想象一副被数十年练习打磨光滑的嗓音。

abstract.en: Picture a friendship with visible stitching, mended each time it frayed.
abstract.cn: 想象一段带着明显针脚、每次磨损都被补好的友谊。

examples.en: The cultivated slope supports three crops a year, while the wild one supports none.
examples.cn: 这块被耕作的坡地一年能种三季，而荒地一季也没有。

examples.en: Cultivated mushrooms are grown on sterilised straw.
examples.cn: 栽培蘑菇种在消过毒的秸秆上。

examples.en: His cultivated manner made even bad news easier to hear.
examples.cn: 他有教养的举止让坏消息也变得容易听进去。

dict_mnemonic.text: cultivate（耕作、培养）+ -ed（已完成）→ 已被耕过的、已被培养成的；土地、植物、细胞、人与品味都能用。

root: cultivate + -ed；cultivate 来自中世纪拉丁 cultivare「耕作」，再上溯 cultiva「耕过的土地」与 colere「耕作、居住、敬奉」，更早词根属重构形式。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one participle: what people have worked on carries the mark of that work, whether it is soil, a crop, a cell, a person, a taste, a skill or a tie.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿同一个分词展开：凡被人经手照料过的东西都带着那份劳作的印记，无论是土壤、作物、细胞、人、品味、技能还是关系。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a field with straight rows and a person with measured speech are both surfaces that show the marks of long care.
core.cn: 核心意象：行距笔直的田与说话有分寸的人，都是显示出长期照料痕迹的表面。

branches.en: THE GROUND: the participle's oldest and most literal use.
branches.cn: 土地：这个分词最古老、最字面的用法。

branches.en: THE PLANTS: field crops and garden stock, both chosen and tended by people.
branches.cn: 植物：田间作物与园中种苗，都由人选择并照料。

branches.en: THE DISH: laboratory growth is cultivation made visible under glass.
branches.cn: 培养皿：实验室里的生长是隔着玻璃可见的培育。

branches.en: THE PERSON AND THE SKILL: polish of manner and training of ability.
branches.cn: 人与技能：举止的优雅与能力的训练。

branches.en: TASTE AND TIES: both are acquired slowly and kept by repetition.
branches.cn: 品味与关系：两者都缓慢获得，并靠重复维持。

intro.en: Cultivated is a participle-adjective, so its parts are the verb cultivate and the ending -ed, with the rest of the family built from the same root.
intro.cn: cultivated 是分词形容词，其组成部分是动词 cultivate 与词尾 -ed，词族其余成员也由同一词根构成。

latinIntro.en: Latin cultivare supplies the verb; the English ending -ed marks the completed state, while -ation, -or, -able and -ar build the related family.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 cultivare 提供动词；英语词尾 -ed 标记完成状态，而 -ation、-or、-able 与 -ar 构成相关词族。

items.example: People cultivate the plant for its oil.
items.exampleCN: 人们为取其油而栽培这种植物。

items.example: The ending turns an action into a finished state.
items.exampleCN: 这个词尾把动作变成完成状态。

items.meaning: the work of tilling or tending
items.example: Cultivation began with the first ploughing.
items.exampleCN: 培育从第一次犁地开始。

items.structure: cultivate + -or (one who acts or a tool)
items.example: The cultivator passes between the rows.
The cultivable strip is only ten metres wide.
items.exampleCN: 可耕种的地带只有十米宽。

items.example: Each cultivar ripens at a different time.
items.exampleCN: 每个品种的成熟时间都不同。

items.example: Uncultivated ground held the old wildflowers.
items.exampleCN: 未开垦的地里留着旧日的野花。

items.example: The recultivated strip yielded a poor first crop.
items.exampleCN: 重新耕作的地带第一季收成很差。

latinEntries.structure: cultivare, cultivavi, cultivatum (verb, first conjugation, Medieval Latin)

definition_zh: 认证；资格认定；认可状态
definition_en: official approval that an institution, course, or person meets a required standard
core_image: 评审团在文件上盖章，宣布这家机构可以开门
scene: 医学院每隔几年要接受一次全面检查，从课程表查到解剖室，通过后才能继续招生。 The school lost its accreditation after the review.
sceneCN: 这里 accreditation 是「认证」（第 1 个义项：官方认定某机构达到标准）；句意为该校在评审后失去了认证资格。

derivatives.zh: 本词的动词形式，义为「认证；委派」
由动词加过去分词后缀构成，义为「获认证的」

senses.title: Official certification
senses.definition: the formal recognition that a body meets a required standard
senses.definitionCN: 正式承认某机构达到规定标准
senses.example: The hospital's accreditation depends on its infection records.
senses.exampleCN: 这家医院的认证取决于其感染记录。
senses.why: The -tion noun names the act of giving trust; accreditation is trust granted in writing after inspection.
senses.whyCN: -tion 名词指「给予信任」的动作；accreditation 就是检查后以书面形式给予的信任。

senses.title: The status granted
senses.titleCN: 获认可的状态；认证资格
senses.definition: the standing an institution enjoys while its approval remains valid
senses.definitionCN: 机构在认可有效期间享有的地位
senses.example: Losing accreditation would bar graduates from licensing exams.
senses.exampleCN: 失去认证资格会让毕业生无法参加执照考试。
senses.why: Once granted, the act becomes a lasting status, and the word shifts from ceremony to standing.
senses.whyCN: 一旦授予，动作就变成持续的状态，词义从仪式转向地位。

senses.title: The review process
senses.definition: the procedure of inspection and decision that leads to approval
senses.definitionCN: 导致批准的检查与决定程序
senses.example: Accreditation took eighteen months and two site visits.
senses.exampleCN: 认证花了十八个月，两次现场考察。
senses.why: The same noun can name the whole drawn-out procedure, from self-study to the final vote.
senses.whyCN: 同一个名词也可指整个漫长的程序，从自评到最终表决。

intro.en: Accreditation is the -tion noun of accredit, so it inherits the Latin trust root credere.
intro.cn: accreditation 是 accredit 的 -tion 名词，继承拉丁语「信任」词根 credere。

items.en: credere meant 'to trust or believe'.
items.cn: credere 意为「信任、相信」。

items.en: creditum meant something entrusted.
items.cn: creditum 意为所托付之物。

items.en: French credit named trust and standing.
items.cn: 法语 credit 指信任与声望。

items.en: English accredit meant to give credit or authority.
items.cn: 英语 accredit 意为给予信用或授权。

items.en: The action suffix named the process of granting that trust.
items.cn: 动作后缀指授予信任的过程。

items.en: Modern usage fixes it in education, hospitals, and laboratories.
items.cn: 现代用法把它固定于教育、医院与实验室。

note.en: The first group gathers verb, participle, and credential words; the second gathers words for formal approval.
note.cn: 第一组收动词、分词与 credential 相关词；第二组收表示正式批准的词。

entries.definition: The verb meaning to certify or send with credentials.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「认证」或「派驻」。

entries.definition: An adjective for an approved institution.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「获认证的」。

entries.definition: A qualification or document proving trust.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「资格证书」。

entries.definition: Formal written confirmation of a standard.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「证明、认证」，对标准的书面确认。

entries.definition: The granting of official permission to operate.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「发照」，授予经营许可。

entries.definition: A general word for official agreement.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「批准」，泛指的官方同意。

entries.definition: Official acknowledgement of status or quality.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「承认」，对地位或质量的正式认可。

normalIntro.en: The normal hooks use the trust root and the review phrases; the abstract hooks picture inspectors walking a corridor with clipboards.
normalIntro.cn: 常规记忆点用「信任」词根与评审搭配；抽象记忆点想象评审员拿着记录板走过走廊。

normal.en: Accreditation is the -tion noun of accredit, so it means the act or status of being trusted.
normal.cn: accreditation 是 accredit 的 -tion 名词，指被信任的动作或状态。

normal.en: Gain accreditation and lose accreditation are the two news patterns.
normal.cn: gain accreditation 与 lose accreditation 是两种新闻搭配。

normal.en: The adjective accredited is more common in daily use.
normal.cn: 形容词 accredited 在日常中更常用。

normal.en: The verb accredit also means to send an official envoy.
normal.cn: 动词 accredit 也指派驻正式代表。

normal.en: In the United States, regional bodies grant it to colleges.
normal.cn: 美国由地区机构向院校授予认证。

abstract.en: Picture inspectors with clipboards walking a teaching corridor.
abstract.cn: 想象评审员拿着记录板走过教学走廊。

abstract.en: Picture a certificate hanging beside a dean's door.
abstract.cn: 想象院长门旁挂着证书。

abstract.en: Picture a graduate barred from an exam because the stamp expired.
abstract.cn: 想象因印章过期，毕业生被挡在考场外。

examples.en: The programme applied for accreditation last autumn.
examples.cn: 该项目去年秋天申请认证。

examples.en: Full accreditation lasts five years.
examples.cn: 完全认证资格有效期为五年。

examples.en: Accreditation requires evidence of student outcomes.
examples.cn: 认证需要学生成果的证据。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「阿克莱迪泰申」——检查过、盖过章，说这家机构可信，就是认证。

root: accredit（给予信任）+ -ation（动作）；核心义是「以书面形式正式给予的信任」

sensesIntro.en: The senses move from the act of certifying, to the standing it grants, to the long review that precedes it.
sensesIntro.cn: 这些义项从认证的动作，走到它给予的地位，再到之前的漫长评审。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a stamped approval that lets an institution open its doors
core.cn: 核心意象：允许机构开门的盖章批准

branches.en: The formal act of recognizing a standard.
branches.cn: 承认标准的正式动作。

branches.en: The standing that remains while approval holds.
branches.cn: 批准有效期间保留的地位。

branches.en: The inspection and decision leading to approval.
branches.cn: 导致批准的检查与决定。

branches.en: The ceremony and the status are two faces of one noun.
branches.cn: 仪式与地位是同一个名词的两面。

branches.en: The review creates the standing and later renews it.
branches.cn: 评审创造地位，并在以后续期。

intro.en: The noun joins the trust root cred- with the action ending -ation, and its family keeps the verb and participle.
intro.cn: 这个名词把「信任」词根 cred- 与动作后缀 -ation 结合，词族保留动词与分词。

latinIntro.en: Latin credere and creditum stand behind the word, so those entries are recorded.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 credere 与 creditum 在该词之后，因此收录这些条目。

definition_zh: 投球手；保龄球玩家；圆顶硬礼帽
definition_en: a person who bowls or delivers the ball in cricket; also a hard round-brimmed hat
core_image: 三幅画面：板球场上助跑投球的球员；球道上掷出保龄球的玩家；绅士头顶那顶圆硬礼帽
scene: 比赛最后一局，全场屏息。 The bowler ran up and delivered the ball at terrifying speed.
sceneCN: 这里 bowler 是「投球手」（第 1 个义项：板球中投球的人）；句意是投球手助跑后以惊人的速度将球投出。

derivatives.zh: 词源基础动词，义为「投球；打保龄球」
由动词加名词后缀构成，义为「保龄球运动」
由复合词加形容词后缀构成，义为「戴圆顶礼帽的」

senses.title: The player who delivers the ball in cricket
senses.definition: the fielding player who bowls the ball to the batter in cricket
senses.definitionCN: 板球防守方负责向击球手投球球员
senses.example: The young bowler took five wickets in his first match.
senses.exampleCN: 这位年轻投球手首场比赛就拿下了五个三柱门。
senses.why: The verb bowl names the act of delivering the ball, and the agent suffix -er attaches to the doer.
senses.whyCN: 动词 bowl 指投球动作，加上表人后缀 -er 即指投球之人。

senses.title: A participant in bowling games
senses.definition: a person who plays tenpin bowling or similar games
senses.definitionCN: 玩十瓶保龄球或类似游戏的人
senses.example: She is the best bowler in our league.
senses.exampleCN: 她是我们联赛里最厉害的保龄球玩家。
senses.why: The same verb bowl covers rolling the ball down the alley, so its player shares the name.
senses.whyCN: 同一个动词 bowl 也指沿球道滚球，其玩家自然共用这个称呼。

senses.title: A hard round-brimmed hat
senses.definition: a man's hat with a hard, rounded crown and a narrow brim
senses.definitionCN: 硬质圆顶、窄帽檐的男式礼帽
senses.example: The banker wore a black bowler to work.
senses.exampleCN: 那位银行家戴着黑色圆顶硬礼帽上班。
senses.why: The hat was named in the nineteenth century for the Earl of Leicester's gamekeepers, after the bowling motion the hard dome resembled in shape.
senses.whyCN: 这顶帽子得名于十九世纪莱斯特伯爵猎场看守人所订制，其硬质圆顶与碗状木球的形似让它随 bowl 一词得名。

senses.title: A shallow dish, as in bowl of a pipe
senses.definition: the rounded hollow part of something, such as a pipe
senses.definitionCN: 器物上圆凹的部分，如烟斗的斗钵
senses.example: He tamped the tobacco into the bowler of his pipe.
senses.exampleCN: 他把烟丝按进烟斗的斗钵里。
senses.why: The image of the rounded wooden ball extends to any rounded hollow, and the -er form survives in dialect use.
senses.whyCN: 圆木球的意象扩展到一切圆凹之物，这一 -er 形式留存于方言用法。

senses.title: A person skilled in delivering anything
senses.definition: figuratively, one who delivers remarks or challenges the way a bowler delivers a ball
senses.definitionCN: 比喻像投球手那样「掷出」言论或挑战的人
senses.example: As a debater he is a fast bowler of hard questions.
senses.exampleCN: 作为辩手，他像一个快投手，接连抛出刁钻问题。
senses.why: The sporting act of hurling at a target maps onto verbal exchange.
senses.whyCN: 朝目标掷球的体育动作被映射到言语交锋上。

senses.title: A symbol of respectability
senses.definition: the hat as an emblem of the respectable city gentleman
senses.definitionCN: 作为城市绅士体面象征的那顶帽子
senses.example: In old films, the bowler marks the city clerk at once.
senses.exampleCN: 在老电影里，圆顶礼帽一出场就点明了都市小职员身份。
senses.why: Because one class wore one hat, the object absorbed the class's meaning.
senses.whyCN: 一个阶层固定戴一种帽子，物品便吸入了阶层的含义。

senses.title: The position or role of bowling in a team
senses.definition: the bowling side or duty within a cricket team
senses.definitionCN: 板球队中负责投球的一方或职责
senses.example: The captain chose him for the bowler role in the final over.
senses.exampleCN: 队长选他在最后一局承担投球任务。
senses.why: A doer's name can stand for the slot that doer occupies.
senses.whyCN: 行为者的名称可转指其占据的位置。

senses.title: A gamekeeper's hat by origin
senses.definition: the hat in its historical sense, designed for gamekeepers on horseback
senses.definitionCN: 该帽的历史本义：为骑马的猎场看守人设计的帽子
senses.example: The bowler was first ordered as headgear for mounted gamekeepers.
senses.exampleCN: 圆顶硬礼帽最初是为骑马的猎场看守人订制的头具。
senses.why: Tracing the word backward keeps alive the profession story inside the object name.
senses.whyCN: 回溯词源，物件名称里那段职业故事得以留存。

intro.en: Bowler is the agent noun of bowl; the hat sense grew in the nineteenth century from the same family.
intro.cn: bowler 是 bowl 的施动者名词；帽子义于十九世纪由同一词族发展而来。

items.en: The verb bowl meant to roll a ball, recorded from the fourteenth century, probably from Old French boule.
items.cn: 动词 bowl 意为滚球，十四世纪已有记录，一般认为源自古法语 boule。

items.en: Old French boule meant a ball, from Latin bulla, a bubble or rounded object.
items.cn: 古法语 boule 意为球，来自拉丁语 bulla（气泡、圆物）。

items.en: Latin bulla meant a bubble or knob; its earlier origin is uncertain.
items.cn: 拉丁语 bulla 意为气泡或圆突；更早来源不确定。

items.en: The agent noun bowler formed from bowl plus -er for the player.
items.cn: 十五世纪由 bowl 加 -er 构成表人名词 bowler。

items.en: In 1849 the hard hat was made for Thomas William Coke's gamekeepers, and bowler hat entered English.
items.cn: 1849 年，为托马斯·威廉·科克的猎场看守人订制了这种硬帽，bowler hat 由此进入英语。

items.en: Modern English keeps the player senses first and the hat sense as a chiefly British usage.
items.cn: 现代英语以「玩家」诸义为主，「帽子」义主要为英式用法。

note.en: Bowler wears two masks at once: the athlete and the hat; spelling twins are few.
note.cn: bowler 一词身兼两相：运动员与帽子；拼写近似词不多。

entries.definition: to roll a ball, or a rounded dish
entries.definitionCN: 滚球；碗；词源基础

entries.definition: the game of rolling balls at pins
entries.definitionCN: 保龄球运动；同根名词

entries.definition: wearing a bowler hat, often of officials
entries.definitionCN: 戴圆顶礼帽的；常指官员形象

entries.definition: a vessel that heats water
entries.definitionCN: 锅炉；与 bowler 仅一字母之差，词源不同

entries.definition: a shady garden retreat
entries.definitionCN: 凉亭；树荫处；拼写相近但词源无关

entries.definition: the player who throws the ball in baseball
entries.definitionCN: 棒球投手；与板球投球手角色对应

entries.definition: one who throws something
entries.definitionCN: 投掷者；泛指投掷之人

entries.definition: a person taking part in a game
entries.definitionCN: 运动员；泛称

entries.definition: a covering for the head
entries.definitionCN: 帽子；bowler 是其具体一种

entries.definition: a tall silk hat, informally
entries.definitionCN: 高顶礼帽（口语）；同为帽子俗称

normalIntro.en: One verb, one suffix, two pictures: bowl gives bowler the athlete and bowler the hat.
normalIntro.cn: 一个动词加一个后缀，两幅画面：bowl 既给了投手 bowler，也给了礼帽 bowler。

normal.en: bowl means to roll a ball in games.
normal.cn: bowl 指比赛中滚球。

normal.en: -er makes the doer, as in player and runner.
normal.cn: -er 构成行为者，如 player、runner。

normal.en: the hat is called bowler after its round bowl-like dome.
normal.cn: 该帽因圆顶如碗（bowl）而得名 bowler。

normal.en: bowling is the alley game with ten pins.
normal.cn: bowling 是十瓶球道的保龄球运动。

normal.en: British English keeps the cricket bowler central.
normal.cn: 英式英语以板球投球手义为核心。

abstract.en: Picture the ball's curve mirrored in the hat's dome.
abstract.cn: 想象球的弧线映在帽子的圆顶上。

abstract.en: One quick delivery decides the over, just as one glance fixes the stereotype.
abstract.cn: 一记快投定乾坤，一如一顶帽子定性一个人。

abstract.en: Roll, release, repeat: the word rolls as smoothly as the ball.
abstract.cn: 滚、出、再滚：这个词像球一样滚得顺滑。

examples.en: The fast bowler rattled the stumps with the very first ball of the innings.
examples.cn: 这位快投手在局首第一球就击中了三柱门。

examples.en: In the city photographs of the period, nearly every clerk wears a bowler.
examples.cn: 那个时期的城市照片里，几乎每个职员都戴着圆顶硬礼帽。

examples.en: Our best bowler rolled three strikes in a row last night.
examples.cn: 我们最棒的保龄球玩家昨晚连投了三个全中。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「抛了」——球「抛了」出去的是投手，头上的硬帽圆得像「抛了」出去的球：bowler 的两副面孔。

root: 中古英语动词 bowl（滚球）+ 施动者后缀 -er；bowl 一般认为源自古法语 boule（球），上溯拉丁语 bulla（气泡、圆物），更早来源不确定。

sensesIntro.en: The doer of the bowling act comes first, then the player of bowling games, and finally the hat whose dome shares the ball's round shape.
sensesIntro.cn: 义项先有投球之人，再有保龄球玩家，最后是圆顶如球的硬礼帽。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a round ball set rolling by a hand, echoed in a round hat
core.cn: 核心意象：一只手把圆球滚出，这圆形又回声般落在圆帽上

branches.en: the cricket arm: the deliverer and the delivery role
branches.cn: 板球一臂：投球者与投球职责

branches.en: the alley arm: the tenpin player
branches.cn: 球道一臂：十瓶球玩家

branches.en: the dome: the hat and its gamekeeper origin
branches.cn: 圆顶：帽子及其猎场看守的来历

branches.en: the uniform of respectability: class written on a hat
branches.cn: 体面的制服：写在帽子上的阶层

branches.en: the rounded hollow and the figurative delivery
branches.cn: 圆凹之物与比喻性的「出手」

intro.en: A transparent agent formation: bowl plus -er, with the hat sense attached by shape rather than by suffix.
intro.cn: 构词透明：bowl 加 -er；帽子义靠形状附着，而非靠后缀。

latinIntro.en: The Latin cognate bulla anchors the family on the continent.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁同源词 bulla 是该词族在欧洲大陆的锚点。

bowler is the one who bowls

items.exampleCN: bulla 衍生出古法语 boule
boule 进入英语成为 bowl

items.exampleCN: hollow 与 bowler 仅音近
