items.exampleCN: boiler 与 bowler 仅差一字母

latinEntries.example: bulla aurea, a golden seal pendant

definition_zh: 谄媚的；阿谀奉承的；吹捧的
definition_en: full of excessive praise meant to please someone important
core_image: 下属弯着腰，把一堆好听的话像糖果一样捧到上司面前
scene: 庆功宴上经理刚举杯，周围已经是一片夸赞声。 The adulatory speech praised the manager far beyond his real contribution.
sceneCN: 这里 adulatory 是「谄媚的、吹捧过头的」（第 1 个义项：言辞上过分讨好的）；句意为奉承的致辞把经理夸得远超他实际的功劳。

derivatives.zh: 由本词去 -ory 加名词后缀构成，义为「吹捧；谄媚」
动词原形，义为「谄媚；奉承」
由动词加施动后缀构成，义为「谄媚者」

senses.title: Excessively flattering in words
senses.definition: expressing admiration that is excessive and meant to please
senses.definitionCN: 表达出过分的赞美，目的是讨好对方
senses.example: The adulatory review read like an advertisement.
senses.exampleCN: 那篇吹捧的评论读起来像广告。
senses.why: The Latin root adulari means 'to fawn like a dog', so the core image is a dog wagging itself into favor.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁词根 adulari 意为「像狗一样摇尾」，核心意象就是摇尾巴讨好人。

senses.title: Servile in manner toward the powerful
senses.definition: showing a servile, fawning attitude toward someone powerful
senses.definitionCN: 对有权势者表现出的低姿态与讨好
senses.example: The staff's adulatory behavior around the chairman made the visitors uneasy.
senses.exampleCN: 员工们在董事长身边那副阿谀的姿态让访客很不舒服。
senses.why: Fawning in words extends to the whole posture: the body language of a courtier.
senses.whyCN: 言辞上的摇尾延伸到整个姿态：廷臣式的肢体语言。

intro.en: Adulatory comes from Latin adulatio, 'fawning', from the verb adulari, 'to fawn like a dog'.
intro.cn: adulatory 来自拉丁语 adulatio（谄媚），动词原形是 adulari（像狗一样摇尾讨好）。

items.en: Adulari meant 'to flatter, to fawn'; its origin within Latin is uncertain.
items.cn: 拉丁语 adulari 意为「奉承、讨好」；它在拉丁语内部的来源不确定。

items.en: Adulatio was the noun for fawning behavior, common in descriptions of court life.
items.cn: 名词 adulatio 指谄媚行为，常见于对宫廷生活的描写。

items.en: English took adulation and adulatory from Latin in the sixteenth century.
items.cn: 英语于十六世纪从拉丁语借入 adulation 与 adulatory。

items.en: The adjective settled into reviews, biographies and political writing for empty praise.
items.cn: 十九世纪前，该形容词固定用于书评、传记与政论文中的空洞吹捧。

items.en: Adulatory now almost always carries a critical tone, suggesting insincere praise.
items.cn: 现代英语中 adulatory 几乎总带贬义，暗示赞美并不真诚。

note.en: The first group gathers words of similar shape; the second gathers near synonyms of flattery.
note.cn: 第一组收词形相近的词；第二组收表示「奉承、讨好」的近义词。

entries.definition: A grown person; only the first letters match, the root is entirely different.
entries.definitionCN: 名词或形容词，义为「成年人；成年的」；只是开头字母与 adulatory 相近，词源完全无关。

entries.definition: To make impure by mixing; shares the ad- prefix only, the rest is a different root.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「掺假」；与 adulatory 只共享前缀 ad-，词干来源不同。

entries.definition: Deep worship or love; the meanings both involve praise, but the roots differ.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「崇敬；爱慕」；虽然同样涉及赞美，但词源与 adulatory 无关。

entries.definition: Flattering powerful people for personal gain.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「谄媚的」，强调为私利讨好权贵。

entries.definition: Servile in manner, eager to obey and please.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「卑躬屈膝的」，偏重姿态上的低声下气。

entries.definition: Showing servile affection, like a dog greeting its master.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「摇尾乞怜的」，保留词源中狗的意象。

normalIntro.en: The hooks use the fawning-dog root and the flattery scene; the abstract hooks picture wagging tails and honeyed words.
normalIntro.cn: 常规记忆点用「摇尾狗」词根与奉承场景；抽象记忆点想象摇动的尾巴与抹了蜜的话。

normal.en: Latin adulari means 'to fawn like a dog'.
normal.cn: 拉丁语 adulari 意为「像狗一样讨好」。

normal.en: Adulation is the noun for such praise.
normal.cn: adulation 是这种吹捧的名词。

normal.en: Adulate is the plain verb form.
normal.cn: adulate 是朴素的动词形式。

normal.en: The ending -ory makes it an adjective.
normal.cn: 词尾 -ory 使它成为形容词。

normal.en: Adulatory praise is never sincere.
normal.cn: adulatory 式的赞美从不真诚。

abstract.en: Picture a dog wagging so hard it spins.
abstract.cn: 想象一条狗摇尾巴摇得原地打转。

abstract.en: Picture a speech dripping with syrup.
abstract.cn: 想象一篇淋满糖浆的致辞。

abstract.en: Picture medals handed out before the work is judged.
abstract.cn: 想象作品还没评审、奖章已经发完。

examples.en: The adulatory speech praised the manager far beyond his real contribution.
examples.cn: 奉承的致辞把经理夸得远超他实际的功劳。

examples.en: Critics dismissed the biography as adulatory and shallow.
examples.cn: 评论家批评这本传记一味歌功颂德、内容肤浅。

examples.en: He grew suspicious of the adulatory tone of the new assistant.
examples.cn: 新助教那副阿谀的腔调让他起了疑心。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「额丢料」——额头都丢出去了（磕头），材料全没了，只剩一肚子奉承话。

root: 拉丁语 adulari（摇尾讨好，来源不确定）→ adulatio（谄媚）→ 英语 adulation / adulatory；核心义是「像狗讨主人那样的赞美」

sensesIntro.en: The senses move from flattering words to the servile manner behind them.
sensesIntro.cn: 义项从言辞上的吹捧，走到背后那副讨好的姿态。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a dog fawning at its master's feet
core.cn: 核心意象：趴在主人脚边摇尾的狗

branches.en: Praise poured far beyond the truth.
branches.cn: 远远越过事实的赞美。

branches.en: The bent posture behind the words.
branches.cn: 话语背后弯下去的腰。

branches.en: Both senses trade dignity for favor.
branches.cn: 两个义项都在用尊严换好处。

branches.en: Reviews and speeches are its usual stage.
branches.cn: 书评与致辞是它常见的舞台。

branches.en: Courts and offices breed this manner.
branches.cn: 宫廷与职场滋生这种姿态。

intro.en: The word carries the Latin flattering root adul- with the adjective ending -ory, and the family gives adulation and adulate.
intro.cn: 这个词带着拉丁语「讨好」词根 adul- 与形容词尾 -ory，同族词有 adulation 与 adulate。

latinIntro.en: Latin adulari and adulatio are the recorded ancestors.
latinIntro.cn: 这里记录的拉丁语 adulari 与 adulatio 是直接祖先。

definition_zh: 决定性的；果断的；确凿的；关键的
definition_en: settling a question or outcome, or showing the ability to decide quickly and firmly
core_image: 一枚砝码落在天平的一端，指针立刻停住，不再摆动
scene: 比赛还剩最后一分钟，他带球突破，一脚把比分定在了终点。 Her decisive goal settled the match.
sceneCN: 这里 decisive 指直接决定了结果（第 1 个义项：决定性的）；句意为她那个决定性的进球定了胜负。

pos.zh: 决定性的；果断的；确凿的

senses.title: Settling the outcome
senses.definition: having the power to settle a contest or question
senses.definitionCN: 具有决定比赛或问题结果的力量
senses.example: Her decisive goal settled the match.
senses.exampleCN: 她那个决定性的进球定了胜负。
senses.why: The Latin verb meant 'to cut off'; a decision cuts away the other possibilities, and a decisive act does so in one stroke.
senses.whyCN: 这个拉丁动词意为「切掉」；决定切掉其他可能，而 decisive 的行为是一刀切完。

senses.title: Able to decide firmly
senses.definition: of a person, able to choose quickly and without hesitation
senses.definitionCN: 指人能迅速选择、毫不犹豫
senses.example: She is decisive under pressure.
senses.exampleCN: 她在压力下很果断。
senses.why: A person who can cut off options does not linger at the fork, and the word praises that speed.
senses.whyCN: 能切掉选项的人不会在岔口徘徊，这个词赞赏的正是这种速度。

senses.title: Conclusive in evidence
senses.definition: of evidence or proof, strong enough to end doubt
senses.definitionCN: 指证据或证明强到足以终结怀疑
senses.example: The fingerprints were decisive evidence.
senses.exampleCN: 指纹是确凿的证据。
senses.why: Proof decides a case the way a verdict decides a trial: once it arrives, argument has nowhere left to go.
senses.whyCN: 证据决定案件，正如裁决决定审判：它一旦出现，争论就无处可去。

senses.title: A battle that ends a war
senses.definition: of a battle or campaign, one that determines the larger outcome
senses.definitionCN: 指决定更大结局的战役或行动
senses.example: The battle was decisive for the whole campaign.
senses.exampleCN: 这场战役对整个战局具有决定性意义。
senses.why: Not every victory changes the war; the word marks the one after which the rest is a formality.
senses.whyCN: 并非每场胜利都改变战争；这个词标记的是那一场之后其余都成形式的胜利。

senses.title: A turning moment
senses.definition: of a moment, the point at which the future is fixed
senses.definitionCN: 指未来在此被固定的时刻
senses.example: That winter was the decisive moment in his career.
senses.exampleCN: 那个冬天是他事业中的关键时刻。
senses.why: Time has joints, and the word names the one where the limb can bend no other way.
senses.whyCN: 时间有关节，而这个词命名的是那个肢体再也不能向别的方向弯曲的关节。

senses.title: A clear advantage
senses.definition: of an advantage, large or well placed enough to guarantee success
senses.definitionCN: 指优势大到或位置好到足以保证成功
senses.example: Air power gave them a decisive advantage.
senses.exampleCN: 空中力量给了他们决定性优势。
senses.why: An advantage is decisive when it cannot be answered by the other side's resources.
senses.whyCN: 当对方的资源无法回应时，优势就是决定性的。

senses.title: A firm tone
senses.definition: of speech, firm and final rather than exploratory
senses.definitionCN: 指言语坚定而最终，而非试探性的
senses.example: He answered in a decisive tone that ended the discussion.
senses.exampleCN: 他用斩钉截铁的语气回答，结束了讨论。
senses.why: Tone can cut a conversation short the way a decision cuts options; nothing is left open.
senses.whyCN: 语气可以像决定切掉选项那样截断对话；没有留下任何开放之处。

senses.title: The determining factor
senses.definition: the element that determines how something else turns out
senses.definitionCN: 决定其他事物如何发展的要素
senses.example: Cost was the decisive factor in the choice.
senses.exampleCN: 成本是这一选择中的决定因素。
senses.why: Among many causes, one is decisive when removing it changes the result.
senses.whyCN: 在众多原因中，当移除某个原因会改变结果时，它就是决定性的。

intro.en: Decisive comes from a Latin verb meaning to cut off, because a decision cuts away alternatives.
intro.cn: decisive 来自一个意为「切掉」的拉丁动词，因为决定就是把其他可能切掉。

items.en: English formed decisive in the 17c. from decision, and applied it to battles, evidence and character alike.
items.cn: 英语在十七世纪由 decision 造出 decisive，并把它用于战役、证据与性格。

items.en: Decisio meant 'a cutting off' and also 'a settlement', the moment when a dispute is cut short.
items.cn: decisio 意为「切掉」，也指「了结」，即争端被截断的那一刻。

items.en: Decidere combined de- 'off' with caedere 'to cut', giving 'to cut off, settle'.
items.cn: decidere 由 de-「离开」与 caedere「切」组合，意为「切掉、了结」。

items.en: Caedere 'to cut' also gives cement, incision and concise, all built on cutting.
items.cn: caedere「切」也产生 cement、incision 与 concise，都以「切」为基底。

items.en: The metaphor widened from legal settlement to character: a decisive person is one who can cut off hesitation.
items.cn: 这个比喻从法律了结扩展到性格：果断的人就是能切掉犹豫的人。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the decision stem; the near-meaning group names kinds of finality.
note.cn: 形近组共享 decision 词干；近义组列出各种终结性。

entries.definition: a choice or a settlement reached.
entries.definitionCN: 作出的选择或达成的了结。

entries.definition: in a way that settles or acts firmly.
entries.definitionCN: 以决定性或果断的方式。

entries.definition: the quality of acting firmly or settling matters.
entries.definitionCN: 行动果断或了结事情的性质。

entries.definition: unable to decide, or not settling anything.
entries.definitionCN: 无法决定，或不能了结任何事。

entries.definition: putting an end to doubt or argument.
entries.definitionCN: 终结怀疑或争论。

entries.definition: having the power to fix how something ends.
entries.definitionCN: 有力量固定事物如何收场。

entries.definition: firm and unwavering in a decision already made.
entries.definitionCN: 对已作的决定坚定不动摇。

entries.definition: at a point where the outcome is decided.
entries.definitionCN: 处于结局被决定的关口。

normalIntro.en: The hooks keep the picture of a blade cutting away every other option.
normalIntro.cn: 下面的联想把「刀刃把其他选项全部切掉」的画面留住。

normal.en: Decide and decisive share the Latin image of cutting off: one stroke, no options left.
normal.cn: decide 与 decisive 共享拉丁语「切掉」的意象：一刀下去，没剩别的选项。

normal.en: Picture a scale that stops swinging the moment the weight lands.
normal.cn: 想象天平在砝码落下的那一刻停止摆动。

normal.en: A decisive person does not stand at the fork counting roads.
normal.cn: 果断的人不会站在岔口数路。

normal.en: Say dih-SY-siv, with the stress on the cut.
normal.cn: 读成 dih-SY-siv，重音落在那一刀上。

normal.en: Link it with conclusive: both end the argument.
normal.cn: 把它和 conclusive 联系：两者都终结争论。

abstract.en: A choice is a cut; hesitation is the blade that will not fall.
abstract.cn: 选择是一次切割；犹豫就是不肯落下的刀。

abstract.en: One cause is decisive when removing it changes everything.
abstract.cn: 当移除某个原因会改变一切时，它就是决定性的。

abstract.en: Finality can live in a tone as well as in a battle.
abstract.cn: 终结性既可以活在战役里，也可以活在语气里。

examples.en: Her decisive goal settled the match.
examples.cn: 她那个决定性的进球定了胜负。

examples.en: The fingerprints were decisive evidence.
examples.cn: 指纹是确凿的证据。

examples.en: Cost was the decisive factor in the choice.
examples.cn: 成本是这一选择中的决定因素。

dict_mnemonic.text: de（离开）+ cis（切）：把其他可能都切掉、只留一个，就是「果断、决定性」。

root: 拉丁语 decidere（切掉、了结）：de-（离开）+ caedere（切）

sensesIntro.en: Decisive always means that alternatives have been cut away; the senses differ in whether the cutting is done by an event, a person, a proof or a cause.
sensesIntro.cn: decisive 始终表示其他选项已被切掉；各义项的差别在于这一刀是由事件、人、证据还是原因落下的。

core.en: ONE CUT ENDS THE DOUBT
core.cn: 一刀结束怀疑

branches.en: Outcomes and battles that settle a larger contest.
branches.cn: 了结更大争夺的结果与战役。

branches.en: The personal and vocal firmness of a decided mind.
branches.cn: 已决之心在个人与语气上的坚定。

branches.en: Proof strong enough to end doubt.
branches.cn: 强到足以终结怀疑的证据。

branches.en: Turning moments and advantages that fix the future.
branches.cn: 固定未来的关键时刻与优势。

branches.en: The one cause whose removal changes the result.
branches.cn: 移除后便改变结果的那个原因。

intro.en: The word belongs to a family built on cutting: decide, decision, decisive and their negatives.
intro.cn: 这个词属于一个以「切」为基础建立的词族：decide、decision、decisive 及其否定形式。

latinIntro.en: Latin caedere 'to cut' supplies a whole set of English words about endings and precision.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 caedere「切」提供了一整组关于终结与精确的英语词。

items.meaning: to cut off options and choose
items.example: They decided to postpone the launch.

items.meaning: the act or result of choosing
items.exampleCN: 决定是一夜之间作出的。

items.example: The indecisive reply cost them the deal.
items.exampleCN: 含糊的答复让他们失去了交易。

definition_zh: 概率；可能性；或然性；概率论；可信度
definition_en: the extent to which something is likely to happen or to be true, or the branch of mathematics that measures it
core_image: 一只骰子在桌上翻滚，六面朝上的机会被写成一个分数
scene: 气象员看着云图，给出明天下雨的可能性很小。 The probability of rain tomorrow is low.
sceneCN: 这里指「某件事发生的可能程度」（第 2 个义项：日常可能性）；句意为明天下雨的可能性很低。可辨识物件：云图、天气图、铅笔、概率标尺。

pos.zh: 概率；可能性；或然性；概率论

senses.title: A numerical measure of chance
senses.definition: a number between zero and one expressing how likely an event is
senses.definitionCN: 取值在零与一之间、表示事件可能程度的数
senses.example: The probability of drawing an ace is one in thirteen.
senses.exampleCN: 抽到王牌的概率是十三分之一。
senses.why: Latin probabilitas named credibility; mathematics narrowed it into a number between nought and one.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁 probabilitas 本指可信程度；数学把它收窄成零与一之间的一个数。

senses.title: The likelihood of an event
senses.definition: how likely something is to happen, in ordinary speech
senses.definitionCN: 日常说法里某件事发生的可能程度
senses.example: The probability of rain tomorrow is low.
senses.exampleCN: 明天下雨的可能性很低。
senses.why: The everyday sense keeps the older meaning of what may reasonably be expected.
senses.whyCN: 日常义保留较古的意思：什么可以合理地预期。

senses.title: The branch of mathematics
senses.definition: the mathematical study of chance and random events
senses.definitionCN: 研究机会与随机事件的数学分支
senses.example: Probability grew out of games of chance in the seventeenth century.
senses.exampleCN: 概率论在十七世纪从赌博游戏里发展出来。
senses.why: The name of the measure became the name of the discipline that studies it.
senses.whyCN: 这个量的名称变成了研究它的学科的名称。

senses.title: Conditional probability
senses.definition: the chance of one event given that another event has occurred
senses.definitionCN: 在另一事件已发生的前提下，某一事件发生的可能
senses.example: Conditional probability changes when the first event is known.
senses.exampleCN: 已知第一个事件之后，条件概率就改变了。
senses.why: Knowledge of one event removes part of the sample space, so the measure is recalculated within what remains.
senses.whyCN: 知道一个事件发生会去掉部分样本空间，于是概率在剩下的范围里重算。

senses.title: A value used in significance testing
senses.definition: the chance of seeing data at least this extreme if the null hypothesis holds
senses.definitionCN: 在原假设成立时，看到至少这样极端的数据的机会
senses.example: A probability below the threshold led the team to reject the null hypothesis.
senses.exampleCN: 概率低于阈值，使研究团队否定了原假设。
senses.why: Testing turns probability into a decision rule: if the chance of the data is small, the assumption is doubted.
senses.whyCN: 检验把概率变成一条决策规则：若数据出现的机会很小，就怀疑那个前提。

senses.title: The phrase 'in all probability'
senses.definition: a fixed phrase meaning that something is almost certain
senses.definitionCN: 一个表示某事几乎确定的固定说法
senses.example: In all probability, the train will be late.
senses.exampleCN: 十有八九，这趟车会晚点。
senses.why: The phrase adds 'all' to the measure in order to say that the likelihood is very high.
senses.whyCN: 这个说法在概率前加「全部」，以表示可能程度非常高。

senses.title: A very small chance
senses.definition: a chance so small that it is worth naming as remote
senses.definitionCN: 小到值得称为「渺茫」的机会
senses.example: There is a probability, though a remote one, that the letter was lost.
senses.exampleCN: 这封信有可能丢失，尽管机会渺茫。
senses.why: English can use the same noun for a low value as for a high one, with a qualifier to mark the scale.
senses.whyCN: 英语可以用同一个名词指低值，也可以指高值，只靠限定词标出高低。

senses.title: Credibility of a statement
senses.definition: the degree to which an account or a claim deserves belief
senses.definitionCN: 一种说法或主张值得相信的程度
senses.example: The probability of her account rests on two witnesses.
senses.exampleCN: 她的说法有多可信，取决于两位证人。
senses.why: The oldest layer of the word is exactly this: what is worthy of approval, before any number is attached.
senses.whyCN: 这个词最古老的一层正是如此：什么值得认可，还没有附上任何数字。

intro.en: Probability comes from Latin probabilitas 'credibility', from probabilis 'that can be approved or proved', from probare 'to test, prove'. It reached English through Old French in the fourteenth century.
intro.cn: probability 出自拉丁 probabilitas「可信」，再上溯形容词 probabilis「可认可、可证明的」，动词为 probare「检验、证明」；十四世纪经古法语进入英语。

items.en: Probare meant 'to test, examine, prove'. It is related to probus 'good, upright', and the pair belongs to an old root of testing and approval, reconstructed rather than directly attested.
items.cn: probare 意为「检验、审查、证明」。它与 probus「好、正直」相关，这一对词属于一个表示「检验与认可」的古老词根，该词根为重构形式，并无直接书证。

items.en: Probus meant 'good, honest, upright', said of people and of quality. The link with probare is generally accepted, though the exact root shape is reconstructed.
items.cn: probus 意为「好、诚实、正直」，可用于人和品质。它与 probare 的联系一般被接受，但确切词根形态属重构。

items.en: Probabilis meant 'that can be approved, credible', and was used of opinions and evidence before it was used of numbers.
items.cn: probabilis 意为「可认可的、可信的」，先用于意见与证据，后用于数字。

items.en: The abstract noun probabilitas named the quality of being credible, the direct source of the English word.
items.cn: 抽象名词 probabilitas 指可信的性质，是英语词的直接来源。

items.en: Old French probabilite carried the noun into English in the fourteenth century, first in the sense of likelihood or plausibility.
items.cn: 古法语 probabilite 在十四世纪把这个名词带入英语，最初指「看似可能」。

items.en: The numerical sense developed with the mathematics of games of chance in the seventeenth century, and the discipline took the word as its name.
items.cn: 数值义随十七世纪赌博数学发展起来，这门学科也把这个词当作名称。

note.en: Group one holds words from the same proving root that are easy to confuse; group two holds words for how likely something is.
note.cn: 第一组是同出「检验、证明」词根、容易混淆的词；第二组是表示「有多大可能」的词。

entries.definition: The adjective for something likely or credible; the noun is its abstract form.
entries.definitionCN: 表示很可能或可信的形容词；名词是它的抽象形式。

entries.definition: Able to be demonstrated by evidence; it comes from prove, which shares the Latin proving root.
entries.definitionCN: 可由证据证明的；出自与拉丁「证明」同根的 prove。

entries.definition: Evidence that settles a question; the noun of result from the same proving root.
entries.definitionCN: 能定论一个问题的证据；同根的结果名词。

entries.definition: Uprightness of character, from probus 'good'; it looks like probability but names a virtue.
entries.definitionCN: 品行的正直，出自 probus「好」；形似 probability，却指一种德性。

entries.definition: The everyday noun for the chance of something, with no mathematical claim.
entries.definitionCN: 表示某事机会的日常名词，不带数学含义。

entries.definition: The possibility that something happens, often spoken informally.
entries.definitionCN: 某事发生的可能，常用于口语。

entries.definition: The ratio between the chances of two outcomes, as in betting.
entries.definitionCN: 两种结果机会之比，常用于博彩。

entries.definition: Something that can happen, with no statement about how often.
entries.definitionCN: 可能发生的事，不说明频率。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real fixed phrases and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实固定说法与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: The root means 'test and approve', so probability began as credibility and only later became a number.
normal.cn: 词根意为「检验与认可」，因此概率最初指可信，后来才变成数字。

normal.en: One family runs probability, probable, probably, probabilistic, improbable and probity.
normal.cn: 同族词串成一条线：概率、很可能的、很可能、概率的、不太可能的、正直。

normal.en: The same proving root gives proof, prove and provable, all about evidence rather than chance.
normal.cn: 同一「证明」词根还给出证据、证明、可证明的，都关于证据而非机会。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the uses: the probability of, in all probability, conditional probability.
normal.cn: 固定说法标出用法：某事的概率、十有八九、条件概率。

normal.en: A probability is a number between nought and one; anything outside that range is not a probability at all.
normal.cn: 概率是零与一之间的数；超出这个范围的就不是概率。

abstract.en: Picture a die rolling across a table, with one face counted and written as a fraction.
abstract.cn: 想象一只骰子在桌上翻滚，某一面被数出来写成一个分数。

abstract.en: Picture a weather map with a shaded band whose width shows how unsure the forecaster is.
abstract.cn: 想象一张天气图，上面一条带阴影的宽带显示预报员有多不确定。

abstract.en: Picture a jury weighing two witnesses, deciding how much credit a story deserves.
abstract.cn: 想象陪审团权衡两位证人，判断一个说法值多少信任。

examples.en: The probability of two heads in a row is one quarter.
examples.cn: 连续两次抛出正面的概率是四分之一。

examples.en: In all probability the meeting will end early.
examples.cn: 十有八九，会议会提前结束。

examples.en: Conditional probability depends on what is already known.
examples.cn: 条件概率取决于已知的情况。

dict_mnemonic.text: 词根意为「检验、证明」，加抽象名词词尾表示「可被认可的性质」：先指说法可信，后指数值化的机会大小。

root: 拉丁 probabilitas「可信」＝ probabilis「可认可的」＋抽象名词词尾，probabilis 出自 probare「检验、证明」，与 probus「正直」同属一个表示「检验与认可」的古老词根，该词根为重构形式。英语十四世纪经古法语传入。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one idea: something is weighed and found more or less worthy of belief. That weighing becomes a number, then a discipline, then a decision rule, and finally any estimate of how likely a claim is to be true.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿同一个观念展开：把某事放在天平上称一称，看它值多少信任。这种称量先变成数字，再变成学科，再变成决策规则，最后指对一种说法为真的可能程度的估计。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a die rolling across a table while a shaded band on a weather map shows how unsure the answer is.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只骰子在桌上翻滚，同时天气图上一条阴影带显示答案有多不确定。

branches.en: A NUMBER: the technical value and the everyday likelihood are one scale, read precisely or loosely.
branches.cn: 一个数：技术数值与日常可能程度是同一把尺，只是读得精或粗。

branches.en: A DISCIPLINE: the study of chance, including the case where part of the answer is already known.
branches.cn: 一门学科：研究机会，包括已知部分答案的情形。

branches.en: TEST RULE: a small probability of the data becomes grounds for doubting an assumption.
branches.cn: 检验规则：数据出现机会很小，就成了怀疑某个前提的理由。

branches.en: SCALE: the same noun can name a near certainty or a remote chance, with a qualifier to mark which end.
branches.cn: 尺度：同一个名词既可指近乎确定，也可指渺茫机会，靠限定词标出哪一端。

branches.en: CREDIBILITY: the oldest layer asks how much belief a statement deserves.
branches.cn: 可信度：最古老的一层问的是一种说法值多少相信。

intro.en: Probability is a Latin abstract noun from a verb of testing; the same root builds the adjectives and the plain verb for proving.
intro.cn: probability 是一个拉丁抽象名词，出自表示检验的动词；同一词根还构成形容词与表示证明的普通动词。

latinIntro.en: Latin probare gives probabilitas, probabilis and probus; the English family includes probable, proof, prove and probity.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 probare 衍生 probabilitas、probabilis 与 probus；英语词族包括 probable、proof、prove、probity。

items.example: The root supplies the idea of testing something before believing it.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根提供「先检验再相信」的意思。

items.example: The adjective adds a moral shade to the same root.
items.exampleCN: 这个形容词给同一词根加上道德色彩。

items.meaning: able to be approved or proved
items.example: The adjective names what passes the test.
items.exampleCN: 这个形容词指能通过检验的东西。

items.example: The noun names the quality, then the measure.
items.exampleCN: 这个名词先指性质，后指度量。

definition_zh: 土生土长的；原住民的；本地原产的；当地固有的
definition_en: originating naturally in a particular place, or belonging to the original people of a region
core_image: 一棵树从本地的土里长出来，根就在这里，不在别处
scene: 这里指「土生土长的」。 The reserve protects plants indigenous to the valley, several of which grow nowhere else.
sceneCN: 这里 indigenous 是「本地原产的」（第 2 个义项：某物种自然生长于某地）；句意：保护区保护本山谷原产的植物，其中几种在其他地方完全不生长。图中可辨识物件：山谷轮廓、贴地生长的灌木、标出边界的围栏。

pos.zh: 土生土长的；原住民的；本地原产的

senses.title: Belonging to the original people
senses.definition: relating to the people who first lived in a region
senses.definitionCN: 与最早居住于某地区的人群相关的
senses.example: The law recognizes indigenous land rights.
senses.exampleCN: 这项法律承认原住民的土地权利。
senses.why: Indigena meant 'born in the place'. The adjective marks people whose origin is in the ground under them, not across a sea.
senses.whyCN: indigena 意为“生在此地”。这个形容词标记的是根在脚下土地而非海外的人。

senses.title: Native to a region's wildlife
senses.definition: in biology, describing a species that evolved naturally in a given area
senses.definitionCN: 生物学中描述在某地区自然演化的物种
senses.example: The garden grows only indigenous shrubs.
senses.exampleCN: 这座花园只种本地原生灌木。
senses.why: A species is indigenous when its line began here. The word is about origin, not about being common.
senses.whyCN: 一个物种若其谱系始于此地，就是本地原产的。这个词讲的是来源，而不是常见与否。

senses.title: Rooted in local culture
senses.definition: describing customs or institutions that developed locally rather than being imported
senses.definitionCN: 描述在当地发展而非输入的风俗或制度
senses.example: The festival is indigenous to the island.
senses.exampleCN: 这个节庆是该岛固有的。
senses.why: Culture is treated like a plant: it grew in this soil, and its roots show it.
senses.whyCN: 文化被当作植物看待：它在这片土壤里长成，根就证明了这一点。

senses.title: Growing from within, not imposed
senses.definition: in development studies, arising from local resources and initiative
senses.definitionCN: 发展研究中由本地资源与主动性产生的
senses.example: They argued for indigenous development rather than imported models.
senses.exampleCN: 他们主张内生发展，而不是照搬外来模式。
senses.why: Here the metaphor is political: what is indigenous grew up here and does not need a scaffold brought from abroad.
senses.whyCN: 这里的比喻是政治性的：内生的东西在这里长成，不需要从国外运来脚手架。

senses.title: A language of the place
senses.definition: describing a language spoken by a region's original inhabitants
senses.definitionCN: 描述由某地区原初居民使用的语言
senses.example: The school teaches two indigenous languages.
senses.exampleCN: 这所学校教授两种本地语言。
senses.why: A language is the deepest root a community has. The word says its grammar was formed here.
senses.whyCN: 语言是一个共同体最深的根。这个词说它的语法是在此地形成的。

senses.title: Naturally present in the ground
senses.definition: describing minerals or materials found naturally in a place rather than brought in
senses.definitionCN: 描述在当地天然存在而非输入的材料或矿物
senses.example: The pigment is made from indigenous clay.
senses.exampleCN: 这种颜料由本地黏土制成。
senses.why: The oldest sense is geological: the material was formed under this ground and has never travelled.
senses.whyCN: 最古老的义项是地质性的：材料在这片土地下形成，从未旅行过。

senses.title: Born and raised in the place
senses.definition: describing a person born and raised in a particular region
senses.definitionCN: 描述在某地区出生并长大的人
senses.example: He is indigenous to the highlands.
senses.exampleCN: 他是高地土生土长的人。
senses.why: This is the literal core: a person born in the place. It is neutral about politics and simply states origin.
senses.whyCN: 这是字面核心：生在此地的人。它对政治中立，只陈述来源。

senses.title: Local as opposed to imported
senses.definition: describing what belongs to a place as distinct from what was introduced
senses.definitionCN: 描述属于本地、区别于外来引入的事物
senses.example: Local farmers prefer indigenous breeds.
senses.exampleCN: 当地农民偏爱本地品种。
senses.why: The word always draws a border. On one side are things grown here; on the other, things carried in.
senses.whyCN: 这个词始终画一条边界。一边是在此地长成的东西，另一边是被搬进来的东西。

intro.en: Indigenous comes from Latin indigena, 'a native, one born in the country'. It is built from an old form of in- plus gignere, 'to beget, to give birth'. The word therefore means 'born here', and every sense tests where a thing's origin lies.
intro.cn: indigenous 来自拉丁语 indigena“本地人、本地出生者”。它由 in- 的古体加 gignere“生育、产生”构成。因此这个词意为“在此出生”，每个义项都在检验某物的来源在何处。

items.en: The root behind gignere, 'to beget', is reconstructed as *gen-, 'to give birth, to produce'. It is generally accepted and also underlies genus, generate and kin.
items.cn: gignere“生育”背后的词根被重构为 *gen-“生育、产生”，一般被接受，也是 genus、generate 与 kin 的来源。

items.en: Gignere meant 'to beget, to cause to be'. Its related noun genus named a birth-line or kind. The two words gave English a whole family of origin words.
items.cn: gignere 意为“生育、使存在”。其相关名词 genus 指血统或种类。两个词为英语提供了一整族关于来源的词。

items.en: Indu- is an archaic form of in-, preserved in indigena. The identification of indu- with in- is generally accepted but rests on comparison rather than direct record.
items.cn: indu- 是 in- 的古体，保存在 indigena 中。把 indu- 认定为 in- 一般被接受，但依据是比较而非直接记录。

items.en: Indigena meant 'native, born in the place'. It was used of people, animals and plants alike, which is why the English word covers all three.
items.cn: indigena 意为“本地的、在此出生的”，既用于人，也用于动物与植物，这就是英语这个词同时覆盖三类对象的原因。

items.en: English borrowed indigenous in the 17th century as a learned word for 'native'. Early writers applied it to plants before peoples.
items.cn: 英语在 17 世纪借入 indigenous 作学术词，意为“本地的”。早期作者先把它用于植物，后用于人群。

items.en: Indigenous peoples became the standard international term for the original inhabitants of a region, carrying legal claims about land and self-government.
items.cn: indigenous peoples 成为国际上指某地区原初居民的标准说法，承载关于土地与自治的法律主张。

note.en: The look-alike group separates the noun for a person, the abstract noun and the verb of making local. The meaning group compares words for belonging to a place.
note.cn: 形近组区分指人的名词、抽象名词与“使本土化”的动词；词义组比较表示“属于某地”的词。

entries.definition: a person or organism native to a region. It is the countable noun behind the adjective.
entries.definitionCN: 某地区原生的个人或生物。它是形容词背后的可数名词。

entries.definition: the quality of being indigenous. It is used in academic and political writing.
entries.definitionCN: 土生土长的性质。它用于学术与政治写作。

entries.definition: to make something local in character. It is the active form of the adjective's idea.
entries.definitionCN: 使某物具有本地特征。它是形容词观念的活动形式。

entries.definition: belonging to a place by birth. It is the everyday near-synonym and can also mean 'innate'.
entries.definitionCN: 因出生而属于某地。它是日常近义词，也可指“天生的”。

entries.definition: relating to the earliest known inhabitants. It is close to sense 01 but is used especially of Australia and Canada.
entries.definitionCN: 与已知最早居民有关的。它接近第 1 义项，尤用于澳大利亚与加拿大。

entries.definition: found only in one region, often of a species or disease. It stresses restriction, while indigenous stresses origin.
entries.definitionCN: 仅见于某一地区，常用于物种或疾病。它强调限定，而 indigenous 强调来源。

entries.definition: belonging to a particular neighbourhood or district. It is broader and carries no claim about origins.
entries.definitionCN: 属于某一街区或地区的。它更宽，不含关于起源的主张。

normalIntro.en: These hooks build indigenous from indu- plus gignere, 'to be born', and keep the image of a tree whose roots never left this soil.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩从 indu- 加 gignere“生育”搭起 indigenous，并保留“树根从未离开这片土”的意象。

normal.en: See gignere: born. Indigenous means born in this place, not brought here.
normal.cn: 看见 gignere：出生。indigenous 意为在此地出生，而非被搬来。

normal.en: Picture a tree whose roots are visible in the local soil and go nowhere else.
normal.cn: 想象一棵树，根就露在本地土壤里，哪里也不去。

normal.en: Compare with exotic: indigenous grew here, exotic was carried in.
normal.cn: 与 exotic 对照：indigenous 是在此长成，exotic 是被搬进来。

normal.en: An indigenous language keeps its grammar in the ground of the community.
normal.cn: 本地语言把语法留在共同体脚下的土里。

normal.en: Remember the family: genus, generate and native all come from the same 'birth' root.
normal.cn: 记住词族：genus、generate、native 都出自同一个“出生”词根。

abstract.en: Keep one image: a border drawn around a place, and everything inside it that grew there.
abstract.cn: 只记一个意象：围绕某地画一条边界，边界内一切在此长成的东西。

abstract.en: Treat the word as a question about origin, not about quality.
abstract.cn: 把这个词当作关于来源的问题，而不是关于品质的问题。

abstract.en: Notice that the same adjective defends a plant, a language and a legal right.
abstract.cn: 注意同一个形容词可以为一株植物、一种语言和一项法定权利辩护。

examples.en: The museum works closely with indigenous communities.
examples.cn: 这家博物馆与原住民社区密切合作。

examples.en: Several indigenous species are now threatened by the dam.
examples.cn: 几种本地原生种如今受到大坝威胁。

examples.en: The programme supports indigenous knowledge in medicine.
examples.cn: 该项目支持医学领域的本土知识。

dict_mnemonic.text: 谐音“印地真牛死”：印度本地土生土长的牛真厉害——土生土长的、原产的。

root: 拉丁语 indigena“本地出生者”，由 indu-（in- 的古体，“在内”）加 gignere“生育”构成；核心义为“在此地出生、根在此地”。

sensesIntro.en: Indigenous always asks one question: where did this begin? A people, a shrub, a festival, a development strategy, a language, a clay deposit, a person and a breed are all tested against the same border. Whatever grew inside the border is indigenous; whatever was carried across it is not.
sensesIntro.cn: indigenous 始终在问一个问题：这东西起源于哪里？一个民族、一株灌木、一个节庆、一种发展战略、一门语言、一处黏土矿、一个人、一个品种，都用同一条边界来检验。在边界内长成的是 indigenous；被搬过边界进来的不是。

core.en: Born and grown inside a place, with roots that never crossed the border.
core.cn: 在某地出生、长成，根从未越过边界。

branches.en: PEOPLE: the original inhabitants and a person born in the region.
branches.cn: 人：原初居民与在此地出生的人。

branches.en: NATURE: species and materials formed in this ground.
branches.cn: 自然：在这片土地上演化或形成的物种与材料。

branches.en: CULTURE: customs and languages shaped locally.
branches.cn: 文化：在当地成形的风俗与语言。

branches.en: DEVELOPMENT: growth from local resources and initiative.
branches.cn: 发展：由本地资源与主动性产生的成长。

branches.en: CONTRAST: what belongs here against what was imported.
branches.cn: 对照：属于此地之物与输入之物。

intro.en: Indigenous is indu- plus gignere plus -ous. The items below show the birth family and the forms built directly on this adjective.
intro.cn: indigenous 是 indu- 加 gignere 再加 -ous。下列条目展示“出生”词族，以及直接建立在这个形容词上的形式。

latinIntro.en: The Latin entries give the native noun, the begetting verb and the archaic prefix. Together they spell out 'born inside'.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语条目给出本地人名词、生育动词与古体前缀。三者合起来拼出“生于其内”。

items.example: The olive is indigenous to the region.

items.exampleCN: 最先征询的是本地居民。

items.example: The court debated the meaning of indigeneity.
items.exampleCN: 法庭辩论了原住性的含义。
这一作物是本地培育的。

items.example: Indigenization of the syllabus took years.
items.exampleCN: 教学大纲的本土化花了多年。

items.example: They questioned the indigenousness of the breed.
items.exampleCN: 他们质疑这一品种的原生性。

items.structure: Latin nativus, from nasci 'to be born'
items.example: She is a native speaker of the language.
items.exampleCN: 她是这门语言的母语者。

definition_zh: 名称；称号；称呼
definition_en: a name or title that identifies a person or thing
core_image: 贴在身上的名字牌：一个称呼被郑重地安放到人或物的身上
scene: 新酒庄开张那天，庄主向众人宣布了酒的名字。 The appellation on the bottle told exactly where the grapes were grown.
sceneCN: 这里 appellation 是「名称、产地命名」（第 2 个义项：正式的名称或标识）；句意为：瓶身上的命名标明了葡萄的产地。

derivatives.zh: 同根词，由 appellare（呼唤）发展，义为「呼吁；上诉」
同根派生，义为「上诉的；受理上诉的」
加形容词后缀 -ive，义为「命名的；通名的」

senses.title: A name given to a person
senses.definition: a title or descriptive name attached to a person
senses.definitionCN: 附加在某人身上的称号或描述性名称
senses.example: She earned the appellation of iron chancellor.
senses.exampleCN: 她赢得了铁血首相的称号。
senses.why: To call someone by a name is the root act, so personal titles come first.
senses.whyCN: 用名字称呼某人是最根本的动作，所以个人称号排第一。

senses.title: A formal identifying name
senses.definition: an official or formal name marking what something is or where it comes from
senses.definitionCN: 标明某物身份或来源的正式名称
senses.example: The region's appellation guarantees the wine's origin.
senses.exampleCN: 该产区的命名保证了葡萄酒的来源。
senses.why: Calling a thing by its proper name extends the calling act to labels and marks.
senses.whyCN: 以专名呼唤一物，使「呼唤」的动作延伸到标签与标识上。

senses.title: A word or phrase used in naming
senses.definition: a word or expression that functions as a name in speech or writing
senses.definitionCN: 在口语或书面中充当名称的词语
senses.example: Genius is a grand appellation for a young writer.
senses.exampleCN: 对一个年轻作家来说，天才是个了不得的称呼。
senses.why: The name itself becomes an object we can quote, discuss, or admire.
senses.whyCN: 名字本身成为可引用、可讨论、可赞叹的对象。

senses.title: A classifying label
senses.definition: a general term that places a thing in a category rather than identifying it singly
senses.definitionCN: 把事物归入类别而非单独指认的通名
senses.example: Tree is an appellation covering many species.
senses.exampleCN: 树是涵盖许多物种的通名。
senses.why: Calling can sort as well as single out, giving the class-name sense.
senses.whyCN: 呼唤既能单独指认也能分类排序，于是产生通名义。

senses.title: A nickname or byname
senses.definition: an informal or affectionate name used instead of the real one
senses.definitionCN: 代替真名使用的非正式或亲昵称呼
senses.example: The appellation Shorty stuck with him for years.
senses.exampleCN: 小矮个这个绰号跟了他好多年。
senses.why: People also call each other by invented names, so nicknames join the family.
senses.whyCN: 人们也会用自创的名字互相称呼，绰号因此归入此族。

senses.title: A legal or official designation
senses.definition: the precise name by which a person or entity is designated in documents
senses.definitionCN: 文件中对人或实体指定的精确名称
senses.example: The contract listed her full appellation.
senses.exampleCN: 合同列出了她的完整称谓。
senses.why: Documents demand the exact calling name, adding a formal register.
senses.whyCN: 文件要求确切的称呼名，于是有了正式语体。

senses.title: A title of honor or shame
senses.definition: a name that carries praise or blame onto its bearer
senses.definitionCN: 给承受者带来赞誉或贬责的名号
senses.example: Traitor is an appellation no soldier wants.
senses.exampleCN: 叛徒是士兵都不想要的名号。
senses.why: Names carry feeling, so an appellation can honor or wound.
senses.whyCN: 名字承载情感，称谓因此可以荣耀人也可以刺伤人。

senses.title: A geographical origin name
senses.definition: a protected name showing the geographic origin of a product, especially wine
senses.definitionCN: 标示产品地理来源的受保护名称，尤指葡萄酒
senses.example: Champagne is a protected appellation in Europe.
senses.exampleCN: 香槟在欧洲是受保护的产地命名。
senses.why: Because calling fixes identity, place names became protected appellations.
senses.whyCN: 由于命名固定身份，地名便成为受保护的产地命名。

intro.en: Appellation descends from Latin appellare, to address or call upon, through the noun appellatio, a naming.
intro.cn: appellation 源自拉丁语 appellare（称呼、呼唤），经名词 appellatio（命名）传承而来。

items.en: The reconstructed root *pel- meant to thrust or drive, later Latin pellere.
items.cn: 重构词根 *pel- 意为「推动、驱使」，后成拉丁语 pellere。

items.en: Appellare, ad- plus pellere, meant to drive toward, hence to address someone by name.
items.cn: appellare 由 ad- 加 pellere 构成，本义「向……驱使」，引申为「以名字称呼某人」。

items.en: Appellatio meant a naming or designation, both of persons and of things.
items.cn: appellatio 意为命名、称谓，既指人也指物。

items.en: appellation kept the naming sense and the legal calling sense in medieval French.
items.cn: appellation 在中世纪法语中保留命名义与法律传唤义。

items.en: English borrowed appellation in the fifteenth century, first in legal use.
items.cn: 英语于十五世纪借入 appellation，最初用于法律语境。

items.en: It now names any title or designation, including protected wine origin names.
items.cn: 如今它泛指任何称号或命名，包括受保护的葡萄酒产地名称。

note.en: Appellation shares its root with call-words and overlaps with naming synonyms.
note.cn: appellation 与同根「呼唤」词族共享词源，并与命名类近义词交叠。

entries.definition: relating to courts that hear appeals
entries.definitionCN: 与受理上诉的法院有关的

entries.definition: an earnest request or a request to a higher court
entries.definitionCN: 恳求；上诉

entries.definition: relating to naming; a common noun as a name
entries.definitionCN: 命名的；作名称用的普通名词

entries.definition: a name describing rank, position, or a work
entries.definitionCN: 头衔；标题

entries.definition: an official name or description
entries.definitionCN: 正式名称；指定

entries.definition: a personal name or nickname
entries.definitionCN: 名字；诨名

normalIntro.en: Use the appellare family to fix appellation in memory.
normalIntro.cn: 利用 appellare 词族把 appellation 记牢。

normal.en: appellation = appeal + -ation: the act of calling becomes a name.
normal.cn: appellation = appeal + -ation：呼唤的动作变成名字。

normal.en: Same root as appellate court, both from Latin appellare, to call.
normal.cn: 与 appellate court 同根，都来自拉丁语 appellare（呼唤）。

normal.en: Wine labels use appellation for origin names, e.g. Champagne.
normal.cn: 酒标用 appellation 表示产地命名，如香槟。

normal.en: Ad- (toward) + pellere (drive): driving a name toward someone.
normal.cn: ad-（朝向）+ pellere（驱使）：把名字驱向某人。

normal.en: Pair it: earn the appellation of hero.
normal.cn: 记搭配：earn the appellation of hero（赢得英雄称号）。

abstract.en: Picture a brass nameplate being nailed onto someone's door.
abstract.cn: 想象一块铜名牌被钉上某人的家门。

abstract.en: The name tag floats down and sticks to a bottle of wine.
abstract.cn: 名字牌飘落，贴上一瓶葡萄酒。

abstract.en: Appellation sounds like 'a pal nation' — everyone in the pal nation has a title.
abstract.cn: appellation 听着像 a pal nation——伙伴国里人人都有称号。

examples.en: The city deserved its appellation as the pearl of the north.
examples.cn: 这座城市无愧于北方明珠的称号。

examples.en: Under the appellation of hereditary king, he ruled for decades.
examples.cn: 他以世袭国王的名号统治了几十年。

examples.en: Scholars debated whether the appellation was accurate.
examples.cn: 学者们争论这个称呼是否准确。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「阿婆蕾申」——阿婆举着蕾丝花边的名牌给你命名，谐音仅助记，别当词源。

root: 拉丁词根 pell-（驱使、推动）：ad-（朝向）+ pellere 构成 appellare（呼唤、称呼），其名词 appellatio 即「命名、称号」，进入法语后由英语借为 appellation。

sensesIntro.en: From the act of calling someone by name, appellation expands to formal names, class labels, nicknames, legal designations, honorific or shaming titles, and protected origin names.
sensesIntro.cn: 从「以名呼唤」的动作出发，appellation 依次铺开到正式名称、归类标签、绰号、法律称谓、褒贬头衔以及受保护的产地命名。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a name being solemnly attached to a person or thing
